Por Francisco Verdu A; Arquitecto MArch

https://www.pontblanc.eu/news-briefs/g3608yiz9iuaol8g0w3415euyqvf17-wp536-g52h4-5z74h-bhn2e-zz9p2-3hap7-pr4ha-pregj-azwrn-mjgcp-fkedh-86hee-wgrp6-n9rks

Fecha: 18 de noviembre de 2026, 16:43 h CET (Madrid)

La tranquilidad de hacer algo hoy por el futuro de tus hijos

Cuando todo cambia tan deprisa, da tranquilidad saber que has hecho algo concreto por el futuro de tus hijos. Que, vivan donde vivan, tengan una base en Madrid y algo propio sobre lo que construir.

Hace unos años asesoré a una familia de Chile en la compra de un piso junto a la Castellana: un piso precioso, fachada noble, tres balcones y mucha luz. Desde el principio decidimos que la vivienda estuviera a nombre de sus tres hijos, todos residentes fuera de España.

Los padres eligieron la propiedad conmigo y actuaron mediante poderes otorgados por sus hijos. Organizarlo llevó algo más tiempo, pero permitió dejar la titularidad definida desde la compra.

Hoy, los tres hijos tienen una parte de su patrimonio en Madrid, valorada en euros y en el contexto seguro y estable de la Unión Europea. Esta semana volvimos a hablar para afinar su estrategia de alquiler.

Esta semana miro el mercado, las dificultades de acceso de los jóvenes y una exposición que recuerda por qué también importa el entorno cultural en el que crecen las familias.

Pensar en el futuro no es solo acumular patrimonio: es darle una estructura y un propósito.

The Latest from Pontblanc

La Selección Pontblanc reúne viviendas con una ubicación excepcional y una arquitectura exquisita. Elegidas por el disfrute que ofrecen hoy y por el valor que protegen para el futuro.

Clave Privada de Acceso: PB2026

Top 3 noticias

1. Menos compraventas no significan mejores precios

Detalles clave

Las compraventas de viviendas inscritas en septiembre descendieron un 13,4 % interanual, según los datos provisionales publicados por el INE el 17 de noviembre [1]. El registro recoge operaciones escrituradas con anterioridad, por lo que no mide exactamente la actividad del mes.

Implicaciones

Para una compra familiar a largo plazo, una desaceleración general no basta para concluir que los precios van a bajar. Compararía el precio solicitado con operaciones cerradas (Portal de Notarios), la calidad del edificio y las posibilidades de uso de los hijos dentro de diez o veinte años.

2. La dificultad de comprar cambia las decisiones de los jóvenes

Detalles clave

Un análisis publicado el 16 de noviembre aborda cómo la dificultad para acceder a la vivienda lleva a algunos jóvenes a asumir inversiones financieras de alto riesgo con la esperanza de reunir el capital necesario para comprar [2]. Es una señal de presión sobre las expectativas de acceso, no una recomendación de inversión.

Implicaciones

Tener capacidad para pagar una cuota hipotecaria no significa disponer del ahorro inicial y de los gastos de adquisición. Si una familia quiere ayudar a sus hijos, estudiaría con tiempo si conviene comprar directamente a su nombre, aportar capital o conservar la titularidad de los padres: las consecuencias fiscales, legales y de control son distintas.

3. El Prado conecta poesía y pintura española

Detalles clave

El Museo del Prado presenta desde el 17 de noviembre una exposición sobre Rilke y el arte español, coincidiendo con el centenario de la muerte del poeta [3]. La propuesta explora el diálogo entre literatura y pintura.

Implicaciones

Una casa en Madrid puede ser también una puerta de entrada a una vida cultural compartida entre generaciones. Al elegir ubicación, me importa tanto la arquitectura del inmueble como lo que la familia podrá hacer y descubrir a pocos pasos de casa.

item.title: PANW Stock Surges 8% Overnight: Palo Alto Networks CEO Sees ‘Hundreds Of Billions Of Dollars’ Opportunity In Open-Weight AI Models Security
item.author: StockTwits Inc; Shivani Kumaresan
item.description:
PANW Stock Surges 8% Overnight: Palo Alto Networks CEO Sees ‘Hundreds Of Billions Of Dollars’ Opportunity In Open-Weight AI Models Security
2026-11-19
Por StockTwits Inc; Shivani Kumaresan
https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/panw-stock-palo-alto-networks-ceo-open-weight-ai-security-applied-compute/cNbLCSDR9ik
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Palo Alto Networks (PANW) stock jumped 8% overnight after a third-quarter (Q3) earnings beat, as CEO Nikesh Arora highlighted a market worth billions for securing open-weight AI models. Speaking on the Q3 earnings call, Arora outlined the company's Applied Compute acquisition, which aims to expand enterprise AI security and bring in $1 billion in annual recurring revenue by fiscal 2029.
Palo Alto Networks’ stock is on track for a second straight weekly gain.
Arora said during the Q3 earnings call that businesses are opting for AI models that give them greater ownership and control over their technology. Open-weight models have gained traction, making up more than 60% of token usage, compared with less than 5% a year earlier.
“When organizations put AI at the center of their operations, they want to retain control of their proprietary data, institutional judgment and competitive edge inside their own 4 walls. We expect a future with a serving opportunity in the hundreds of billions of dollars when enterprise applications are driven by open weight and open source adoption.”
To address the enormous security opportunity, Arora said Palo Alto Networks examined potential partners across the AI industry before selecting Applied Compute, citing its engineering capabilities and experience in developing open-weight models through post-training. Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire Applied Compute in an all-stock deal valued at $4.5 billion.
The Palo Alto-Applied Compute deal will focus on two things. Networks plans to integrate AI into its existing cybersecurity products, developing more than 35 specialized applications that will help customers counter AI-led threats with AI-driven defenses.
The second focus will be developing and delivering secure, sovereign versions of open-weight models for enterprise customers. “To support our efforts, we plan to build out a diversified global influence capability of north of 100-plus megawatts over the next 3 to 5 years,” Arora said.
“This will be supported by a modest CapEx commitment at least – of less than $3 billion through fiscal 2030, representing approximately half a year of our annual free cash flow.”
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock improved to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ territory. The stock recorded an 884% surge in message volume over the past 24 hours.
A user said, “Applied Compute acquisition to bolster PANW’s enterprise capabilities in open-weight AI models.”
Another user said, “$PANW agreed to pay $4.5B in stock for Applied Compute, which helps companies customize and run AI models. That’s a pretty big bet that the folks who buy their cybersecurity will also trust them to help run the models. I’d like to see how many customers sign up for both.”
PANW stock has gained 84% year-to-date.
Read Next: Why Did DIS, TGT, ASO Stocks Surge To 52-Week Highs Today?
For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com.
Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages.

item.title: A diversified investment strategy is not just prudent – it is essential
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
A diversified investment strategy is not just prudent – it is essential
2026-11-19
Por Texto propio
A diversified investment strategy is not just prudent – it is essential
By Elias Nechachby
A year ago investors were bracing themselves for a year of uncertainty, upheaval and market volatility driven by conflicts, elections and other economic challenges around the world. Twelve months later, as we look to 2025, the picture is even more challenging.
While global rallies have benefited the equity markets around the world, valuations are now richer, and risks are bubbling under the surface.
Investors interested in shoring up their portfolios are likely attentive to the increased geopolitical risks following the new US presidency, and escalations of war across Russia and the Middle East.
The VIX Index, one of the most popular measures of expected stock market volatility, has had several big spikes in 2024 and is expected to continue to surprise investors in 2025. So, finding a way to manage expected market volatility will be critical for securing robust returns – and peace of mind.
Geopolitical, trade and economic risks
Looking forward, the febrile geopolitical, trade and economic backdrop points to greater volatility. And with some stock valuations over-extended, any upset could lead to a sizeable correction and in the worst case to a hard landing.
For example, the prospect of the US imposing import tariffs on goods from Canada, Mexico and China – its three biggest trading partners apart from the EU – would have ramifications for global businesses and their supply chains. It would also likely have inflationary, currency and other economic repercussions, all of which could have other unforeseen and unwelcome consequences.
So, finding a way to manage expected market volatility will be critical for securing robust returns – and peace of mind.
Confronted with that challenge, investors need to look carefully at their investment strategy to try and insulate their portfolio – after all, robustness is not achieved by chance.
Engineering investment learnings
Diversification is more often than not depicted as the diversification of assets, countries, sectors or stocks to insulate your portfolio against risk.
However, this type of diversification is insufficient as it only works in mild local market corrections, and does not work during global crises such as the 2008 global financial crisis (GFC) or 2020 Covid-19 pandemic.
As a starting point, to insulate their portfolio against potential risks, even though they may not be apparent in the short to medium term, investors need to look beyond the classic asset classes, sector, and country diversification, which notoriously fail to provide investors with any kind of protection during a severe crisis, when all correlations jump to one.
The traditional 60/40 stocks and bonds investment strategy saw a disastrous 2022, declining 17 per cent, with both asset classes seeing downward swings.
As an ex-aeronautical engineer, I approach risk in terms of ‘independent redundancy’. What I mean here is that an investment strategy needs to have several ‘engines’ that allow it to navigate different types of markets, and generate performance whether the market is up, down or flat.
Each ‘engine’ should be truly independent, or else there is an increased risk that they will all fail to perform at the same time. In aeronautics, you have to prove that the likelihood of undetected error for any critical system (that is, ‘the integrity’) is less than one in a billion. To reduce the probability of error and to reach that figure, one must have enough built-in independent redundancies.
That is why investors should look to diversify sources of alpha. Spreading investments across independent performance engines reduces exposure to concentrated risks, and benefit from varying growth opportunities and market dynamics, particularly as US trade policies, tax regulations, and global geopolitical shifts add
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Palo Alto Networks CEO just dropped a truth bomb on the network outages sweeping through major companies
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Palo Alto Networks CEO just dropped a truth bomb on the network outages sweeping through major companies
2026-11-19
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/palo-alto-networks-ceo-just-dropped-a-truth-bomb-on-the-network-outages-sweeping-through-major-companies-101129581.html
Palo Alto Networks CEO just dropped a truth bomb on the network outages sweeping through major companies
A cybersecurity CEO offers plain talk on the outages sweeping through major companies and disrupting everything from your email to your flight.
"I want to be clear, there are two distinct parallel effects that are driving this environment. The first effect is a massive surge in vulnerabilities and patches being deployed. We're seeing critical and severe vulnerabilities discovered nearly seven times the monthly average of last year. These discoveries are happening at a speed and intensity which is hard for IT teams to cope with," Palo Alto Networks (PANW) CEO Nikesh Arora said on his earnings call Wednesday evening.
Added Arora, "We believe many of the major disruptions of the last few weeks, including outages across major enterprises and governments, were partially due to unintended consequences of patching and configuration changes, as IT teams simply cannot patch these vulnerabilities fast enough without compromising their production environments. The second effect is the rise of AI-assisted cyberattacks. Bad actors are using open-weight models and new agentic frameworks to find and exploit vulnerabilities at unprecedented speed and scale. New agentic frameworks like ARTEX are enabling bad actors to turn simple instructions into autonomous, multi-stage attacks, allowing a handful of operators to compromise dozens of targets simultaneously. As we look ahead, we anticipate an elevated threat environment."

item.title: Alibaba's AI Ambitions Face Steep Challenge in US Chip Controls
item.author: Jeanny Yu
item.description:
Alibaba's AI Ambitions Face Steep Challenge in US Chip Controls
2026-11-19
Por Jeanny Yu
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/alibaba-ai-ambitions-face-steep-000021461.html
(Bloomberg) -- Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. (BABA) is facing mounting pressure to show it can deliver on its artificial intelligence business plan despite new limits on its access to data center chips.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Its Hong Kong-listed shares capped a nine-day losing streak ahead of results due later Thursday from the internet firm. Alibaba's market value stands at $216 billion, less than half its level just over a year ago when investors were betting on it to lead the China's AI industry.
Draft US rules announced Monday would close a key workaround for Chinese hyperscalers to use advanced chips. That's making analysts turn more cautious on Chinese AI companies' cloud growth potential as well as their ability to train and run next-generation models.
"For Alibaba, they depend heavily on access to computing power, so this will be an important setback," said Matt Maley, chief market strategist at Miller Tabak. "It's likely going to create a situation where it will take longer for them to build an ecosystem that can compete with the most advanced American technology."
The new US rules are aimed at preventing Chinese firms from renting cutting-edge chips at data centres abroad. Alibaba and its peers are already banned from direct buying the most advanced processors, and Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) said this week it is no longer shipping lower-end Hopper data center chips to China as well.
Part of Alibaba's ambition to build 20 gigawatts of data center capacity before 2032 depends on expansion across regions like Southeast Asia. Chips made in house by its T-Head unit may provide some buffer, but still trail the performance of Nvidia's top products.
Fresh challenges aside, Alibaba's results are expected to show a continued drag on its e-commerce business from sluggish Chinese consumption and tough competition. Focus will be on whether that can be offset by its fast-growing cloud operation, which accounted for 18% of total revenue in the June quarter.
Among its peers, Tencent Holdings Ltd. posted results after Wednesday's close showing a negative profit impact from heavy AI spending. The company also warned that Washington curbs on Chinese access to overseas data centers will hamper development of its next AI model.

item.title: T.J. Maxx owner's secret weapon: Catering to last-minute gift buyers
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
T.J. Maxx owner's secret weapon: Catering to last-minute gift buyers
2026-11-19
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/tj-maxx-owners-secret-weapon-catering-to-last-minute-gift-buyers-110000933.html
It's an unwelcome but familiar feeling: You've run out to the store the week of Christmas to buy the gifts you neglected to get during the entire month of December. But now the toy aisles are bare, nothing on the racks is in the right size, and Amazon can't deliver the gadget your nephew asked you for until after the holiday.
Don't fret. TJX (TJX), the parent company of T.J. Maxx, Marshalls, and HomeGoods, has planned for this. They know you're a late gift buyer. They've got you covered.
CEO Ernie Herrman said part of the company's success in recent years is its fresh inventory, which is updated later into December than at other brick-and-mortar retailers.
"We create an opportunity for a consumer that doesn't want to go online and wants something fresh when a lot of stores are picked over," Herrman said on the company's earnings call Wednesday. "They can come into TJ Maxx or Marshalls and find something there that is just landing 10 days before Christmas, which I think is really groundbreaking in terms of the approach from what other retailers do."
TJX stock surged 9% after posting impressive quarterly results, exceeding expectations and upgrading its full-year outlook on expectations of strong holiday demand for its discount shops.
Follow Hamza Shaban on X @hshaban.

item.title: UnitedHealth and other insurance stocks drag down the Dow after CMS proposes new anti-fraud rule
item.author: Grace O'Donnell
item.description:
UnitedHealth and other insurance stocks drag down the Dow after CMS proposes new anti-fraud rule
2026-11-19
Por Grace O'Donnell
https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/article/unitedhealth-and-other-insurance-stocks-drag-down-the-dow-after-cms-proposes-new-anti-fraud-rule-173851810.html
Healthcare stocks fell again on Wednesday after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) proposed a new rule that would toughen oversight of Medicare, Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP), and the health insurance marketplace.
Sagging shares of managed care providers weighed on the Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI). UnitedHealth Group stock (UNH), one of the Dow's largest components with a 4.32% weighting, fell by more than 10%. Humana (HUM) dropped 13%. Cigna (CI) shares declined by 3%. CVS Health (CVS), which is in the process of splitting up its retail and insurance businesses, fell 5%.
Read more: Medicare out-of-pocket costs are rising in 2027
The rule, called the Comprehensive Regulations to Uncover Suspicious Healthcare, or CRUSH, would increase audits of insurance providers and allow CMS to recover improper payments. It would also require providers to report changes to enrollment information within 30 days, among other conditions.
In the release shared on Monday, officials pointed to bad actors billing Medicare for nonexistent wheelchairs, enrolling healthy seniors in Medicare-funded hospice care, and signing people up for Marketplace plans without their consent as examples of the kinds of fraud this rule aims to crack down on.
CMS said the rule could save taxpayers nearly $90 billion over the next 10 years. The proposal is open to public comment until Jan. 19, 2027.
However, Oppenheimer analysts said they expect the proposal to face similar legal scrutiny to that of a framework a federal court struck down in 2025. Furthermore, the team noted that the $90 billion cost savings likely reflect CMS recouping repayments rather than broad savings to healthcare programs.
"We believe CMS will be subject to the same legal challenges that it faced in 2025," the analysts wrote. "The substantially larger collection estimate reflects broader auditing, with recoveries concentrated in 2028–2030. This is a proposed rule, so CMS could choose to make adjustments in the final rule. Even if the rule were implemented as is, and it were upheld by the courts, we believe plans would incorporate the prospective cost into bids rather than absorb an unchanged recurring earnings burden."

item.title: Trump is greeted by Xi Jinping and meets with Canada’s Mark Carney as the China leg of his Asia trip gets underway
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Trump is greeted by Xi Jinping and meets with Canada’s Mark Carney as the China leg of his Asia trip gets underway
2026-11-19
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/in-china-trump-is-greeted-by-xi-jinping-and-meets-with-canadas-mark-carney-131412638.html
Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomed President Trump with a rare in-person greeting Wednesday in Shenzhen for the Chinese leg of Trump's Asia trip this week.
The Chinese leader even offered Trump a hug, kicking off a visit expected to be dogged by questions of US changes to semiconductor export controls and the ongoing scandal at Nvidia. Trade talks with China and Canada are also on the agenda.
The greeting came ahead of two closely watched sit-down meetings Thursday between Trump and Xi on economic issues and another with Russian President Vladimir Putin joining the conversation.
Trump landed in Shenzhen at 4:42 p.m. local time on Wednesday to a red carpet welcome ceremony, a military band playing the Star-Spangled Banner, and a military flyover, according to a pool report.
The pomp mirrored Trump's tarmac greeting for Xi in the United States in September.
Trump also met with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum later on Wednesday. Carney posted on X that the leaders discussed efforts to reach a trade deal and "agreed to continue the work and to stay in close contact."
The meeting follows significant trade war escalations that erupted between the US and Canada earlier this fall. Recent weeks have seen a new round of talks aimed at reaching a deal to reduce current duties and avert a threatened 50% tariff on Canadian cars, trucks, and auto parts, scheduled to take effect in 2027.
In his own stops ahead of the meeting, Carney announced progress toward lessening trade restrictions with China and Mexico and also claimed that Canada's growing trade relationship with China is not a major concern for Trump.
"We have been making progress," Carney said of talks with the US, but that any deal needs to be "in the interest of Canadians."
Sheinbaum posted a photo of her sitting down with Trump and said it had been "a very good meeting."
A day of opening ceremonies
During Wednesday's whirlwind series of stops, Trump and Xi joined a group photo as the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) fully kicked off.
Trump crossed paths with Putin at the festivities, shaking hands and exchanging pleasantries with the Russian leader. The president then participated in a banquet before returning to his hotel for the night.
The gathering this week had been set to focus on digital trade and artificial intelligence, but the scandal at Nvidia (NVDA) and potential changes to US semiconductor export rules are hanging over it.
The Trump administration published new proposed export limits as Trump departed Washington, a move that was immediately felt in the region.

"We have been making progress," Carney said of talks with the US, but that any deal needs to be "in the interest of Canadians."
Sheinbaum posted a photo of her sitting down with Trump and said it had been "a very good meeting."
A day of opening ceremonies
During Wednesday's whirlwind series of stops, Trump and Xi joined a group photo as the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) fully kicked off.
Trump crossed paths with Putin at the festivities, shaking hands and exchanging pleasantries with the Russian leader. The president then participated in a banquet before returning to his hotel for the night.
The gathering this week had been set to focus on digital trade and artificial intelligence, but the scandal at Nvidia (NVDA) and potential changes to US semiconductor export rules are hanging over it.
The Trump administration published new proposed export limits as Trump departed Washington, a move that was immediately felt in the region.

item.title: Anthropic IPO: Why token usage could become a key metric for AI investors
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Anthropic IPO: Why token usage could become a key metric for AI investors
2026-11-19
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/anthropic-is-betting-big-that-ai-token-usage-will-surge-heres-why-that-matters-for-investors-145557721.html
With Anthropic (ANT) heading toward the public markets on Thursday, industry watchers say AI token usage could become an increasingly important metric for investors, much like subscriber counts were for video streaming services. But they also warn that token usage remains an opaque measure to assess.
Most of Anthropic's revenue comes from customers paying based on how much they use its AI models, a pricing structure the frontier lab describes in its IPO filing as "metered in tokens and priced according to the model selected." A token is a small chunk of text, roughly a short word or part of a word, that an AI model reads or generates.
In an amended filing this month, Anthropic reported $33.2 billion in revenue for the first nine months of 2026, up from $16.3 billion in the first half of the year. During the first six months, consumption-based revenue, which is tied to customer usage and measured in tokens, accounted for roughly 80% of sales, while subscription-based revenue made up the remaining 20%.
Industry bulls point out that even as token prices have fallen across the industry, lower model rates can make AI cheaper to use, thereby driving higher consumption. AI frontier lab: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar recently noted higher usage after cutting prices on Luna, its cheapest model series.
"We saw use go up 10x," Friar said last month. "So that tells you there's a lot of price elasticity of demand right now."
Anthropic said in its filing that a growing number of business customers have signed multiyear contracts with minimum-spend commitments that cannot be canceled and with locked-in pricing. Even with those contracts, Anthropic only books revenue as tokens are actually consumed.
But without total token volume or data showing how much Anthropic actually earns per token, industry watchers point out investors cannot tell how much growth comes from discounted enterprise commitments versus steady demand or how much committed spending remains unused.
This is where Claire Husson-Citanna, founder of Bondcoins and formerly FX swap line principal at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, sees an opportunity: Investors would likely reward labs that disclose not just how much customers have prepaid in token credits, but also how much they actually use and how future revenue and costs are expected to grow.
That visibility matters as cheaper open-weight rivals and advances in quantum computing threaten to put downward pressure on token prices, even as Anthropic faces commitments of nearly $900 billion in long-term computing and infrastructure spending.

item.title: Bill Gurley says giving away AI is Google's 'No. 1' move against Anthropic
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Bill Gurley says giving away AI is Google's 'No. 1' move against Anthropic
2026-11-19
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/bill-gurley-says-giving-away-ai-is-googles-no-1-move-against-anthropic-133314859.html
Bill Gurley, the venture capitalist behind an early bet on Uber (UBER), has an idea for how Google could slow Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) down: Give the AI away.
Gurley, a general partner at Benchmark, told Deirdre Bosa Live on Monday that Alphabet's (GOOGL) Google should use free AI to keep Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) and OpenAI (OPAI.PVT) from pulling away. Anthropic prices its IPO Wednesday and begins trading Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT.
"If Google recognizes that Anthropic ... and OpenAI maybe are getting escape velocity away from them, it is the No. 1 thing they should go do ... bar none," he said.
Gurley calls it playing defense. Open-weight models, which anyone can download, run and change for free, keep one company from locking up a market. Google did it with Kubernetes "when they were worried about Amazon and AWS," he said, and with Android "when they were worried about Apple having a monopoly in phones."
The catch? "We're not seeing those actions from Google."
Open-source AI is winning the traffic
Free models already do most of the work. On OpenRouter, a marketplace developers use to reach hundreds of AI models, seven of the 10 most-used models last week came from Chinese labs and are free to download. DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash alone processed about 77 trillion tokens, the basic units of text that AI models read and write. That's more than the other nine combined.
Duolingo (DUOL) CEO Luis von Ahn told Yahoo Finance last week that open models cut the cost of each AI video call to less than a cent from about 30 cents. "The vast majority of our usage of AI will be in open-weight models pretty soon," he said.
Closed AI is still winning the money
The money flows the other way. Closed models handled 28% of OpenRouter's tokens in mid-September but collected 73% of the spending, according to its September report. Similarly, Apple's (AAPL) iPhone accounted for about a fifth of phones sold in the second quarter but generated nearly half of revenue, according to Counterpoint Research.
Price is a big reason. Anthropic lists Claude Opus 5.5, its most-used model, at about 27 times what DeepSeek charges for its own. And while 39 companies sell DeepSeek's model on OpenRouter, nobody sells Claude Opus for less than Anthropic does. As Gurley put it, "The marginal price is going to equal marginal cost."
Gurley also called Anthropic's choice to write off model training costs right away, rather than over years, "pretty amazing," adding, "it's still profitable, really high gross margin."

item.title: Why Nvidia doesn't need a 'big splashy hire' to replace Jensen Huang as CEO
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Why Nvidia doesn't need a 'big splashy hire' to replace Jensen Huang as CEO
2026-11-19
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/why-nvidia-doesnt-need-a-big-splashy-hire-to-replace-jensen-huang-as-ceo-154424603.html
Maybe Nvidia (NVDA) doesn't need a big free-agent CEO signing to replace highly visible founder and former CEO Jensen Huang.
"If you don't bring Jensen back, I would not hire an outsider," Amazon (AMZN) founder and former CEO Jeff Bezos said at a Semafor conference on Tuesday. "Nvidia is too complicated. I think outside CEOs in complex companies have a vanishingly small chance of succeeding."
Bezos makes a good point.
A new CEO often comes in and runs the standard playbook from an MBA class: Do a listening tour with employees to better understand the business. Meet with the existing C-suite to see who they want to keep and who should get pushed out.
Six months into the job, the new CEO unveils a splashy growth plan that often includes profit-boosting layoffs.
And away they go.
The thing is, Nvidia doesn't need any of this playbook inserted into its unique culture Huang created. It also doesn't need its important operations disrupted by a meddling new CEO seeking praise from the world.
At best, Nvidia needs an internal CEO hire — someone with Huang's technical prowess who could sell the sizzle to a global audience.
At worst, it needs a big-name veteran CEO who promises the board no major overhauls, just small tweaks where needed. That person stays in the job for a few years and establishes a strong succession plan — one that Huang never whipped up.
For his part, Bezos and his board named then-AWS leader and longtime Amazon exec Andy Jassy to succeed him as CEO in 2021.
"I don't think it needs a big splashy hire. I think they have incredible bench strength in there," investor and "Shark Tank" star Kevin O'Leary said on Sozzi Unleashed. "I think they have a tremendous amount of engineers designing the next two generations of chips. I think it's a machine unto itself right now."
Interim CEO Colette Kress made a solid case late Tuesday for staying in the interim CEO role for perhaps longer than Wall Street expects. The company's third quarter was solid, the outlook strong, and Kress came across as a steady hand driving the Nvidia rocketship.
For the third quarter, Nvidia posted adjusted earnings of $2.68 a share on revenue of $115.8 billion. Wall Street had expected earnings of $2.47 a share on revenue of $109.15 billion.
Nvidia expects fourth quarter revenue of $127.4 billion to $132.6 billion, comfortably above the $125.25 billion analysts were looking for.
The company said it sees fiscal year 2028 revenue growth of 75%, up from a prior estimate of 70% offered just three months ago.

item.title: Ford is ‘officially in the battery business’ as first Fathom cells ship - built on Chinese tech
item.author: Pras Subramanian
item.description:
Ford is ‘officially in the battery business’ as first Fathom cells ship - built on Chinese tech
2026-11-19
Por Pras Subramanian
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/ford-is-officially-in-the-battery-business-as-its-first-fathom-cells-ship--built-on-chinese-tech-185120961.html
Ford (F) announced on Wednesday that the first lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery cells are coming off the line at its BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, as part of a plan to license China's CATL battery designs. The move comes against the complicated backdrop of using Chinese tech in US made components.
The batteries are headed to Ford's Louisville Assembly Plant in Kentucky to power prototypes of the Fathom, Ford's upcoming midsize electric pickup. Ford hopes to build an EV cheap enough to win over gas truck buyers, with the Fathom set to start under $30,000 — and key to that is using lower-cost batteries.
"Ford is officially in the battery business. We'll be the first to deliver LFP batteries in the US for mainstream consumer automotive use, and I couldn't be prouder of the Ford team," CEO Jim Farley said on X.
LFP batteries don't use nickel or cobalt, which Ford said helps hold down costs, and the chemistry holds up over years of charging. Ford went with prismatic, or rectangular, cells that fit directly into the chassis. That makes the battery pack part of the truck's structure and cuts costs.
Ford said the Michigan lines can produce 40 cells per minute, making them among the fastest LFP prismatic lines outside China.
But the technology inside those cells produced some controversy.
Ford said its search for a proven LFP design "led us to the world's leading battery manufacturer, CATL," the Chinese giant whose batteries power 30 million vehicles globally. Ford called the deal a "limited technology-licensing and services agreement," not a joint venture. It says it owns the plant, controls operations, and employs the workforce.
That hasn't satisfied Washington. In a letter to Farley sent in early September, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy expressed "profound concern" over Ford's "reliance on technologies of foreign adversaries." He cited the CATL tech in Marshall, Ford's joint factory with Geely in Spain, and its talks with BYD on hybrid components.
Chief communications officer Mark Truby called it a "head-scratcher of a letter" that came "a week after [the] White House touted the very same job-creating Michigan project he's questioning."
Ford's official response called the letter a "wrongheaded attempt to capture headlines."
With that in the rearview mirror (for now), Ford plans to have its battery pack plant in Marshall running in 2027, ahead of the Fathom's launch. Ford said what it learns there will also feed Ford Energy, its battery energy storage business, which is preparing production in Glendale, Kentucky.

The batteries are headed to Ford's Louisville Assembly Plant in Kentucky to power prototypes of the Fathom, Ford's upcoming midsize electric pickup. Ford hopes to build an EV cheap enough to win over gas truck buyers, with the Fathom set to start under $30,000 — and key to that is using lower-cost batteries.
"Ford is officially in the battery business. We'll be the first to deliver LFP batteries in the US for mainstream consumer automotive use, and I couldn't be prouder of the Ford team," CEO Jim Farley said on X.
LFP batteries don't use nickel or cobalt, which Ford said helps hold down costs, and the chemistry holds up over years of charging. Ford went with prismatic, or rectangular, cells that fit directly into the chassis. That makes the battery pack part of the truck's structure and cuts costs.
Ford said the Michigan lines can produce 40 cells per minute, making them among the fastest LFP prismatic lines outside China.
But the technology inside those cells produced some controversy.
Ford said its search for a proven LFP design "led us to the world's leading battery manufacturer, CATL," the Chinese giant whose batteries power 30 million vehicles globally. Ford called the deal a "limited technology-licensing and services agreement," not a joint venture. It says it owns the plant, controls operations, and employs the workforce.
That hasn't satisfied Washington. In a letter to Farley sent in early September, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy expressed "profound concern" over Ford's "reliance on technologies of foreign adversaries." He cited the CATL tech in Marshall, Ford's joint factory with Geely in Spain, and its talks with BYD on hybrid components.
Chief communications officer Mark Truby called it a "head-scratcher of a letter" that came "a week after [the] White House touted the very same job-creating Michigan project he's questioning."
Ford's official response called the letter a "wrongheaded attempt to capture headlines."
With that in the rearview mirror (for now), Ford plans to have its battery pack plant in Marshall running in 2027, ahead of the Fathom's launch. Ford said what it learns there will also feed Ford Energy, its battery energy storage business, which is preparing production in Glendale, Kentucky.

item.title: Jensen Huang and Howard Lutnick will appear publicly before a powerful Senate panel
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Jensen Huang and Howard Lutnick will appear publicly before a powerful Senate panel
2026-11-19
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/jensen-huang-and-howard-lutnick-will-appear-publicly-before-a-powerful-senate-panel-192842634.html
The flood of Capitol Hill interest in the ongoing scandal at Nvidia (NVDA) could create a traffic jam of high-profile hearings in the weeks ahead, including closely watched public grillings by the Senate's powerful banking panel of two of the figures at the center of ongoing national security questions.
A source in Sen. Tim Scott's office confirmed to Yahoo Finance on Wednesday that both ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Lutnick have agreed to appear publicly before the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs, as talks continue over the precise timing.
Scott said on CNBC earlier on Wednesday that he wants to get the testimony done "before Christmas." He had previously requested in a letter that Huang appear on Dec. 3 and Lutnick appear on Dec. 10.
The Commerce Department previously confirmed Lutnick's willingness to appear before the Senate panel, but the confirmation that the testimony will be public — in front of reporters and cameras — sets up what is expected to be one of Washington's most highly anticipated business-world hearings in years as both men face questions about Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy and whether the Trump administration did enough in response to apparent attempts to evade US export controls of advanced semiconductor chips.
The questions will come from Republicans and Democrats, including ranking member Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the committee, who is expected to take the committee's gavel in 2027 when Democrats assume control of the chamber.
Warren has previously accused Huang of "putting our national security at risk" and has promised investigations of her own.
Another Democrat on the panel is Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona, who this week posted "slow your roll there" in response to Huang saying he would be honored to return to the company.
Multiple probes into 'a potential breach of our national security'
That hearing is just one on the congressional calendar.
Huang and Nvidia's top lawyer have also agreed to appear in a closed-door hearing before a trio of House committees.
That joint effort by the House's Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select committees is set to meet behind closed doors with Huang on Dec. 1. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter will then appear in another closed hearing on Dec. 2.
"We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security," Republican Reps. Brian Mast of Florida, John Moolenaar of Michigan, and Rick Crawford of Arkansas said in a joint statement, adding that both interviews will be transcribed.

item.title: Consumers are staying strong as AI stumbles — giving retail stocks fresh appeal
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Consumers are staying strong as AI stumbles — giving retail stocks fresh appeal
2026-11-19
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/consumers-are-staying-strong-as-ai-stumbles--giving-retail-stocks-fresh-appeal-110000718.html
Americans' capacity to spend continues to buoy the economy despite a cost-of-living crunch. The latest measures of consumer retail spending continue a years-long story about cash-strapped households soldering through inflation — and doing so especially as other key parts of the economy look weaker.
As the AI robots stumble, the flesh-and-blood American consumer is still out there on two feet and spending, even if they are looking for deals.
This week's corporate earnings so far show that even though there are bright spots heading into the holiday shopping season, there are still signs of stress and a renewed focus on seeking value above all else.
US retail sales slowed from September but still increased slightly in October, as households pulled back on large purchases like cars and furniture while keeping up spending elsewhere ahead of the holiday shopping season.
Focusing on the underlying strength and resilience of the consumer is easier to do after Target (TGT) posted a standout quarter. The retailer reported a 5% increase in foot traffic, the highest year-over-year jump since January 2022. Net sales jumped slightly more than 7%, with beauty products growing by greater than 9% and food and beverage rising roughly 7%.
Despite inflation and high gas prices, consumers are still swiping and tapping their way through it.
In an interview with Yahoo Finance, Target CEO Michael Fiddelke attributed the company's turnaround success to its fixation on value, an especially potent proposition for consumers in this economy.
"The 'I can't believe the quality of this' or 'I can't believe I found it at Target at a price point' that makes the smile get wider. Once someone turns over the price tag, that's when we're at our best," Fiddelke said.
Inflation's squeeze doesn't always reduce overall spending. It can steer dollars in different directions, influencing how people spend their money.
Home Depot (HD), which posted an earnings beat on Wednesday, said its average ticket size increased by 3% from a mix of higher prices and customers trading up to new and innovative products. But even though transactions were slightly bigger, customers came into the store less often.
"We expect HD will explore price increases in certain categories and lean into cost savings opportunities to navigate this challenging supply chain and broader cost backdrop," Bank of America analysts led by Christopher Nardone wrote in a note earlier this week.
The higher cost of gas and airfare may also juice holiday shopping in a roundabout way.

item.title: Hollywood icon and ‘That ’70s Show’ star could become a billionaire from Anthropic IPO; his firm’s $435M bet is now worth $7B
item.author: Desconocido
item.description:
Hollywood icon and ‘That ’70s Show’ star could become a billionaire from Anthropic IPO; his firm’s $435M bet is now worth $7B
2026-11-19
Por Desconocido
https://parade.com/news/hollywood-icon-and-that-70s-show-star-could-become-a-billionaire-from-anthropic-ipo-his-firms-435m-bet-is-now-worth-7b
The actor’s early bet on artificial intelligence could put him in rare company alongside Tyler Perry, Jerry Seinfeld and Arnold Schwarzenegger.
Nov 18, 2026 9:58 AM EST
Trending News Writer
Follow
FOX / Getty Images
Get Parade in your Google feed
Preferred Source
Google Discover
Ashton Kutcher
could be on his way to billionaire status.
The 48-year-old actor stands to be one of the biggest winners as Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude assistant, prepares to go public at a proposed $1.4 trillion valuation, according to
Page Six
. Sound Ventures, the venture capital firm Kutcher co-founded, has invested about $435 million in Anthropic, and that stake is now reportedly worth about $7 billion, per
Newsweek
Ashton Kutcher’s Anthropic Investment
Sound Ventures first backed Anthropic in 2023, after Kutcher and his business partner Guy Oseary met with the company’s CEO, Dario Amodei,
Bloomberg
reported. The firm kept investing in later rounds and now owns roughly 0.5% of the company.
Kutcher won’t walk away with a $7 billion check, though. Sound Ventures manages money for outside investors, so any profits will be split among several parties.
Ashton Kutcher’s History as a Tech Investor
Kutcher has quietly become one of Hollywood’s most successful tech investors, with a reported net worth of more than $200 million. In 2010, he co-founded A-Grade Investments with billionaire Ron Burkle and Oseary, the longtime manager of
Madonna
and the Red Hot Chili Peppers. Their early bets included Spotify, Uber and Airbnb, and they reportedly grew $30 million into about $250 million, per
Newsweek
Kutcher and Oseary launched Sound Ventures in 2015 as A-Grade’s successor. In July, Kutcher stepped down as a partner but stayed on as a senior advisor.
The Wall Street Journal
reported the decision was partly over differing views on which startups to back: the firm wanted more established companies, while Kutcher prefers early-stage ones. He has since launched a new fund with Morgan Beller, a former co-leader of Meta’s
Libra
project.
Which Actors Are Billionaires?
Musicians such as
Taylor Swift
, Beyoncé and Dr. Dre have reached billionaire status, but it’s far rarer for actors. According to
Forbes
, the film industry’s billionaires include
Tyler Perry
Jerry Seinfeld
and
Arnold Schwarzenegger
Kutcher has been married to his former
That ’70s Show
co-star
Mila Kunis
since 2015. The couple share two children, daughter Wyatt and son Dimitri.
About the author
Clara Awuse
Trending News Writer

item.title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang can nominate two directors to company board, filings show
item.author: Max A Cherney
item.description:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang can nominate two directors to company board, filings show
2026-11-19
Por Max A Cherney
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/former-nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-215939399.html
By Max A. Cherney
SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 17 (Reuters) - Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has the ability to nominate two directors to the Nvidia board ahead of the company's annual shareholder meeting and vote, according to company proxy and corporate filings, giving the co-founder a route to future influence on the company.
Chip industry executives, investors and customers are scrutinizing Nvidia closely to understand what role Huang will play in the company after he resigned as CEO last week. The ability to nominate directors, who choose leadership and provide oversight, could be a powerful tool in influencing the future of the AI chip leader.
Any Nvidia shareholder or group of shareholders that owns more than 3% of the voting power for at least three years is entitled to nominate directors who will be included in the company's proxy materials and vote at its annual meeting, which typically takes place in June.
Huang and entities tied to him have owned more than 3% of Nvidia's shares for more than three years, according to data from LSEG. He currently owns roughly 3.5% of the company.
Huang would be free to nominate anyone who would qualify as an independent member of the board. The candidates would go on Nvidia's proxy ballot.
Nominating board members would not guarantee Huang's allies seats on the company board; shareholders would need to vote to approve potential candidates. Nvidia may also leave a nominee out if the person has violated the company's bylaws and charter.
FOREIGN INTELLIGENCE INVESTIGATION
Nvidia's board said on November 8 that it initiated an investigation in light of recent reporting that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Reuters could not determine if Huang's conduct broke the company's bylaws or charter.
Nvidia and a representative for Huang did not respond to a request for comment.
Since Huang resigned from Nvidia last week in the wake of his extramarital affairs, executives such as Elon Musk, employees, investors and US President Donald Trump have advocated for his return to the top job at the chip designer. The board was not considering reinstating Huang, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Monday.
Huang released a statement on Tuesday and said he "would be honored" to return as CEO if the board decided such a move would be in the best interest of shareholders and employees.
On Tuesday after the market close, Nvidia forecast quarterly revenue above Wall Street estimates, giving investors some relief after the uncertainty caused by Huang's exit.
(Reporting by Max A. Cherney in San Francisco; Editing by Matthew Lewis)

Nvidia's board said on November 8 that it initiated an investigation in light of recent reporting that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Reuters could not determine if Huang's conduct broke the company's bylaws or charter.

Nvidia and a representative for Huang did not respond to a request for comment.

Since Huang resigned from Nvidia last week in the wake of his extramarital affairs, executives such as Elon Musk, employees, investors and US President Donald Trump have advocated for his return to the top job at the chip designer. The board was not considering reinstating Huang, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Monday.

Huang released a statement on Tuesday and said he "would be honored" to return as CEO if the board decided such a move would be in the best interest of shareholders and employees.

On Tuesday after the market close, Nvidia forecast quarterly revenue above Wall Street estimates, giving investors some relief after the uncertainty caused by Huang's exit.

(Reporting by Max A. Cherney in San Francisco; Editing by Matthew Lewis)

item.title: Fed’s Waller doubles down on a jumbo move for December, sees at least two more hikes
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Fed’s Waller doubles down on a jumbo move for December, sees at least two more hikes
2026-11-19
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/feds-waller-doubles-down-on-a-jumbo-rate-hike-in-december-sees-more-hikes-to-come-174616572.html
Federal Reserve governor Chris Waller said Wednesday that if the central bank hikes interest rates by a quarter point next month, it will need to signal that the Fed will hike again by that much in January.
Otherwise, the Fed needs to raise rates by a jumbo half percentage point in December.
"People have argued, do you do 50 in December, nothing in January, or 25 in December, 25 in January," Waller said in an interview Wednesday on CNBC. "But when you do 25 now and you're going to do 25 in January, it only affects market pricing if you signal you're going to do it, and you give the markets a credible signal."
Waller said that if you leave the market guessing about a January rate increase, there won't be an effect on the market and, by extension, the economy.
"If you're not going to signal this very clearly to markets you're going in January, my view is then you have to go 50 in December," Waller said.
Read more: How the Fed rate decision affects your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments
That sounds a lot like forward guidance, which Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has sought to eliminate since taking the reins in May. Warsh has said that telegraphing future policy moves distorts market signals and boxes in policymakers.
But Warsh's philosophy hasn't quite taken hold, as other Fed members have continued to offer clues about the path ahead — which has also led to more questions and at times confusion in markets.
Without using the term explicitly, Waller argued Wednesday that the Fed would need to use forward guidance if it doesn't deliver a jumbo hike next month. He said the central bank could signal its next move either in the statement or at Warsh's press conference. He added that quarterly interest rate projections, which will be released in December, would be helpful this time because it's the end of the year and the projections would be for all of next year.
Waller said the Fed needs to be more aggressive because inflation is moving higher after remaining above the central bank's 2% goal for nearly six years.
Read more: How to protect your savings against inflation
Waller first hinted at a jumbo hike last week, saying ahead of the Consumer Price Index release, that if inflation came in higher than expected, stronger action would be needed.
The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October, compared with expectations of 0.3%. "Core" inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.3%, compared with expectations of 0.2%.
On Wednesday, Waller said the Fed needs to take back the three rate cuts from last year and may need to do more to get inflation to come back down.

item.title: Target's traffic jumps 5%, the biggest gain since 2022, as turnaround brings shoppers back
item.author: Brooke DiPalma
item.description:
Target's traffic jumps 5%, the biggest gain since 2022, as turnaround brings shoppers back
2026-11-19
Por Brooke DiPalma
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/targets-traffic-jumps-5-the-biggest-gain-since-2022-as-turnaround-brings-shoppers-back-130616166.html
Target (TGT) is plotting its comeback, and it's bringing customers back through the doors.
In the third quarter, the retailer posted a 5% increase in foot traffic, the highest year-over-year jump since January 2022. Net sales grew 7.1% to $27.1 billion, driven by more than 9% growth in beauty and roughly 7% growth in food and beverage.
Michael Fiddelke, who became CEO earlier this year, said this could be a good sign for this holiday shopping season, as consumers continue to spend despite inflation and high gas prices.
"One of the most important things is that we're seeing growth driven by traffic," Fiddelke said on a call with reporters. "It's not just one category. It's not just one activation. It's the cumulative impact of all of what we're doing that has [the] guest picking Target more often. That's encouraging as we head into the holiday season, as we build on this momentum in the years to come."
Same-store sales grew by 5.6%, above estimates of 3.7%, driven by customers visiting more often and also spending slightly more when they did.
Chief merchandising officer Cara Sylvester said the company is investing in new food items, which now account for 10% of overall food sales. Sylvester said Target's private-label and national brands are gaining traction as the retailer leans into deals, such as holiday food and beverage items priced at $5 or less.
Beauty is also seeing double-digit growth across skin care, fragrance, hair, and nail care. As of August 2026, Target officially ended its partnership with Ulta, replacing it with its own in-house concept, Target Beauty Studio, which began rolling out this quarter in September.
There is more work to do in apparel and home, though, Fiddelke said.
"We've made progress but are not satisfied with performance," he said. "It was great to see home turn positive in Q3, but we've said that's gonna be a multiyear journey."
Longtime UBS retail analyst Michael Lasser said those categories are "among the clearest sources of untapped upside," but there needs to be "evidence that assortment, merchandising and execution improvements are beginning to translate into better performance."
Sylvester said Target is making a "slow sequence of progress," working on key categories one by one, such as bedding, bath, and women's clothing and shoes. The retailer has seen success with promotions for a $35 faux-fur blanket and a $45 cashmere sweater, similar to Walmart's approach as of late.
Target increased its fiscal 2026 guidance, now expecting net sales to grow 6%, up from its previous forecast of 5%.
Brooke DiPalma is a reporter for Yahoo Finance. Follow her on X at @BrookeDiPalma or email her at bdipalma@yahoofinance.com.

item.title: Fed minutes: Officials favored holding rates steady in October, but they see hikes ahead
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Fed minutes: Officials favored holding rates steady in October, but they see hikes ahead
2026-11-19
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/fed-minutes-officials-favored-holding-rates-steady-in-october-but-they-see-hikes-ahead-195719301.html
Almost all members of the Federal Reserve favored raising interest rates in the future, even as they decided to hold rates steady in October, according to minutes from the central bank's last policy meeting released Wednesday.
"With regard to the outlook for monetary policy in the months ahead, almost all judged that, under their baseline outlooks for inflation and the labor market, further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate — broadly consistent with the September Summary of Economic Projections — would likely be appropriate, in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2% objective," the minutes, which are released with a three-week lag, revealed.
The September Summary of Economic Projections, which includes 18 officials' expectations for the path of interest rates — excluding Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, who doesn't pencil down his — showed one more rate hike this year, then holding rates steady throughout 2027.
Read more: How the Fed rate decision affects your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments
Among those who favored holding rates steady at the last meeting, many said they wanted to gather additional information to help determine the best level of interest rates to bring inflation back down to their 2% goal in a timely way. These officials wanted to assess the durability of AI-related investment demand, the evolution of financing conditions, the transmission of the September rate increase to the economy, and geopolitical developments.
Some said that market expectations for rate hikes in December and next year were broadly consistent with their views on the path of interest rates, and several saw this alignment as reducing the risks of keeping the target range unchanged in October. A few felt holding rates steady was a close call.
Some participants favored raising rates at the last meeting, citing inflation remaining too high with few signs of it abating. They thought rates weren't high enough to restrict the economy and cool inflation, and a few warned that further delay risked allowing high inflation to become entrenched or necessitating a larger and more disruptive tightening later. Cleveland Fed president Beth Hammack, a voting member who publicly dissented last meeting, has made this argument. Fed governor Lisa Cook also dissented last meeting.
Several officials observed that the impact of tariffs on prices appeared to be waning, but most remarked that inflation pressures in the economy were broad-based. The vast majority noted that high energy prices continued to contribute to inflation pressures.

item.title: Bitcoin Erases Bessent Rally as Leverage and Liquidity Fade
item.author: Sidhartha Shukla
item.description:
Bitcoin Erases Bessent Rally as Leverage and Liquidity Fade
2026-11-19
Por Sidhartha Shukla
https://finance.yahoo.com/news/bitcoin-erases-bessent-rally-leverage-094509953.html
(Bloomberg) -- Bitcoin (BTC-USD) has erased all the gains from its late-summer rally as fading risk appetite and the record hack at exchange Binance drove investors to retreat, leaving the largest token trading in a thinner market increasingly vulnerable to sharp price swings.
Liquidity has deteriorated sharply since the hack, meaning large trades can push prices further in either direction. The value of buy and sell orders sitting within 1% of Bitcoin's mid-price, a measure of the liquidity available close to the current price, is down nearly 38% from this year's pre-Binance hack high, according to digital-asset technology firm Talos. Put another way, a large seller may now have to accept lower prices to complete a trade, while a large buyer may have to pay more.
Bitcoin was trading above $64,000 on Wednesday, about 49% below its record high. The selloff since last week has erased the rebound that began in August after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US would increase buybacks of long-dated government debt.
That rally had offered a rare respite for crypto. Digital tokens had struggled to regain momentum since the October 2025 market crash, and Bitcoin's summer advance briefly revived the idea that it could benefit from a "debasement" trade alongside assets such as gold. Recent buyers — holders of coins acquired within the past six months — took heavy losses in early 2026, booked profits during the rally into September and October, and are now selling at a loss again, according to data provider Glassnode.
The backdrop has deteriorated sharply since then. An AI-led equity selloff and a more hawkish Federal Reserve have pushed investors away from riskier assets. The Binance hack then dealt a crypto-specific blow to a market already losing momentum.
"In general, crypto has been at the mercy of the broader risk complex, especially big-tech momentum names all year," said Rajiv Sawhney, head of international portfolio management at Wave Digital Assets. Bitcoin's correlation with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq has risen in recent weeks, he said, suggesting investors are again treating it primarily as a risk asset rather than a haven from currency debasement.
Leverage is also draining from one of crypto's deepest and most actively traded markets. Open interest in Bitcoin perpetual futures, contracts with no expiry date, has fallen to about $41.6 billion, the lowest since November 2024, according to Coinglass, as repeated liquidations of bullish positions drained leverage from the market. About $7.6 billion worth of bullish bets across tokens have been liquidated since the Binance hack.
"Fast money leverage has certainly been exhausted in the system," Sawhney said. But that does not necessarily remove selling pressure. He pointed to miners selling Bitcoin to raise cash as they invest in artificial intelligence and high-performance-computing infrastructure, as well as digital-asset treasury companies facing higher financing costs as the token's prices fall.
Miners MARA and Riot have reported sales of about 60,000 Bitcoin this month as they fund their shift toward AI and data center infrastructure.
The lack of demand for the token is also reflected in exchange-traded funds flows. Investors have pulled about $2.6 billion from US-listed spot Bitcoin ETFs in November so far, removing a source of steady buying that had previously helped support the token.
Jasper de Maere, an OTC trader at Wintermute, said the late summer rebound increasingly looks like a false start. "It is now clear we haven't cleared the bear market yet, and the rally off the July low was a fake-out," he said.

item.content:encoded:
Bitcoin Erases Bessent Rally as Leverage and Liquidity Fade

2026-11-19

Por Sidhartha Shukla

https://finance.yahoo.com/news/bitcoin-erases-bessent-rally-leverage-094509953.html

(Bloomberg) -- Bitcoin (BTC-USD) has erased all the gains from its late-summer rally as fading risk appetite and the record hack at exchange Binance drove investors to retreat, leaving the largest token trading in a thinner market increasingly vulnerable to sharp price swings.

Liquidity has deteriorated sharply since the hack, meaning large trades can push prices further in either direction. The value of buy and sell orders sitting within 1% of Bitcoin's mid-price, a measure of the liquidity available close to the current price, is down nearly 38% from this year's pre-Binance hack high, according to digital-asset technology firm Talos. Put another way, a large seller may now have to accept lower prices to complete a trade, while a large buyer may have to pay more.

Bitcoin was trading above $64,000 on Wednesday, about 49% below its record high. The selloff since last week has erased the rebound that began in August after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US would increase buybacks of long-dated government debt.

That rally had offered a rare respite for crypto. Digital tokens had struggled to regain momentum since the October 2025 market crash, and Bitcoin's summer advance briefly revived the idea that it could benefit from a "debasement" trade alongside assets such as gold. Recent buyers — holders of coins acquired within the past six months — took heavy losses in early 2026, booked profits during the rally into September and October, and are now selling at a loss again, according to data provider Glassnode.

The backdrop has deteriorated sharply since then. An AI-led equity selloff and a more hawkish Federal Reserve have pushed investors away from riskier assets. The Binance hack then dealt a crypto-specific blow to a market already losing momentum.

"In general, crypto has been at the mercy of the broader risk complex, especially big-tech momentum names all year," said Rajiv Sawhney, head of international portfolio management at Wave Digital Assets. Bitcoin's correlation with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq has risen in recent weeks, he said, suggesting investors are again treating it primarily as a risk asset rather than a haven from currency debasement.

Leverage is also draining from one of crypto's deepest and most actively traded markets. Open interest in Bitcoin perpetual futures, contracts with no expiry date, has fallen to about $41.6 billion, the lowest since November 2024, according to Coinglass, as repeated liquidations of bullish positions drained leverage from the market. About $7.6 billion worth of bullish bets across tokens have been liquidated since the Binance hack.

"Fast money leverage has certainly been exhausted in the system," Sawhney said. But that does not necessarily remove selling pressure. He pointed to miners selling Bitcoin to raise cash as they invest in artificial intelligence and high-performance-computing infrastructure, as well as digital-asset treasury companies facing higher financing costs as the token's prices fall.

Miners MARA and Riot have reported sales of about 60,000 Bitcoin this month as they fund their shift toward AI and data center infrastructure.

The lack of demand for the token is also reflected in exchange-traded funds flows. Investors have pulled about $2.6 billion from US-listed spot Bitcoin ETFs in November so far, removing a source of steady buying that had previously helped support the token.

Jasper de Maere, an OTC trader at Wintermute, said the late summer rebound increasingly looks like a false start. "It is now clear we haven't cleared the bear market yet, and the rally off the July low was a fake-out," he said.

"This is a rates tape in which Bitcoin is the non-yielding funding leg, the ETF bid is gone and the technicals have broken," de Maere said, adding every channel "across ETF, DA

item.title: Waymo pulls robotaxis off highways after California ban, with tech seen as 'far from perfect'
item.author: Pras Subramanian
item.description:
Waymo pulls robotaxis off highways after California ban, with tech seen as 'far from perfect'
2026-11-19
Por Pras Subramanian
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/waymo-pulls-robotaxis-off-highways-after-california-ban-with-tech-seen-as-far-from-perfect-161031372.html
The robotaxi rollout in America hit a roadblock.
Alphabet-owned (GOOGL) Waymo pulled its robotaxis off freeways in every US market where it offers them, after California regulators banned the company's driverless cars from state highways.
The move comes as Waymo races to scale its ride-hailing business, where freeway rides are key to growth.
The California Department of Motor Vehicles imposed the restrictions on Nov. 11, though they weren't made public until Tuesday. The agency said Waymo's driverless freeway operations pose an "imminent hazard to public safety," citing "recurring incursions" by its vehicles into active construction zones, per the AP.
According to the DMV, three Waymo vehicles entered an active construction zone on US Highway 101 near Burlingame. In a separate incident, video showed a Waymo trying to pass two California Highway Patrol cruisers on Interstate 280 in San Francisco while officers slowed traffic to clear debris. Waymo said the Highway 101 encounters caused no injuries or collisions.
The ban stays in place until Waymo shows the DMV "effective corrective actions."
A Waymo spokesperson said the company had "temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance." That includes Phoenix, where Waymo launched freeway rides last November alongside San Francisco and Los Angeles.
Yahoo Finance reached out to Waymo for comment but did not immediately hear back.
It's not the first time Waymo pulled service from the highway. In May, seven of its robotaxis drove into active freeway construction lanes in the Bay Area, following similar events in Phoenix in April. Waymo pulled its fleet off freeways and filed a voluntary software recall covering nearly 3,900 vehicles before freeway rides resumed.
Waymo's street coverage is unaffected. Waymo says it handles more than half a million trips a week across 15 US cities, and the map keeps growing.
Last month, Waymo added nearly 250 square miles of service across five cities, including Torrance in Los Angeles, La Jolla in San Diego, and a connection to BART's Berryessa Station in the Bay Area. It also opened rides to everyone in San Antonio, San Diego, and Tampa, and added pickups at Las Vegas' Harry Reid International Airport for existing riders.
Tesla (TSLA) expanded its robotaxi service in Miami recently, as well as Austin.
But the freeway pullback shows that regulators, not companies like Waymo, set the pace of the robotaxi rollout.
"Local regulation is the biggest barrier right now, but that's a good thing," Anthony Townsend, senior research associate at Cornell Tech and author of "Ghost Road: Beyond the Driverless Car," said to Yahoo Finance. "This technology is far from perfect, and right now it's mostly a tool for perpetuating auto dependency."

item.title: Is the AI party over? Anthropic is about to find out.
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Is the AI party over? Anthropic is about to find out.
2026-11-19
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/is-the-ai-party-over-anthropic-is-about-to-find-out-230000591.html
Thursday is supposed to be a celebration of AI.
Anthropic (ANT) is heading toward its long-awaited IPO at the Nasdaq, potentially giving Wall Street one of the biggest new pure-play AI investment stories in years.
Before you hit me up on X, Elon Musk-led SpaceX (SPCX) is not a pure-play AI company. It's an industrial company with a whole lot of AI bolted on.
But there's a problem amid all the Anthropic IPO hoopla.
The very stocks that fueled this AI boom are still under pressure. Just look at the sell-offs this week in top tech names like CoreWeave (CRWV), Salesforce (CRM), and even AMD (AMD).
Read more: Follow along for live updates on the Anthropic IPO
Investors are questioning the AI spending, the valuations, the financing arrangements — and whether the returns will ever justify the billions being poured into this technology.
And the timing couldn't be more fascinating.
Truist chief market strategist Keith Lerner noted that tech valuations have fallen 42% over the past year. The sector has gone from outperforming the S&P 500 (^GSPC) by 25% over six months to underperforming it by 6%. Bank of America's latest fund manager survey shows investors have cut tech exposure by the most since June 2006.
That's a serious reset.
The question pre-Anthropic IPO: Is Wall Street finally getting too negative?
The AI build-out isn't disappearing, as we saw from Nvidia (NVDA) on Tuesday. Companies are still spending. The technology is still evolving. And as Lerner pointed out, previous tech pullbacks of more than 10% during this bull market were followed by an average rebound of 47%.
That doesn't guarantee a repeat. There are real risks — and this AI stock sell-off could get worse.
Anthropic's IPO arrives at a moment when investors are suddenly asking what could go wrong with AI.
Maybe it's time to ask the other question: What could go right?
Investing in Anthropic is like investing in a young Amazon (AMZN), "Shark Tank" star Kevin O'Leary told me on Sozzi Unleashed. Valid point.
Indeed, the biggest opportunity in tech may emerge when Wall Street least wants to own it.
That's the trade I'm watching. Well, that and the first few ticks in ticker symbol ANT!

item.title: AMD, Broadcom, CoreWeave stocks mixed on Nvidia Q3 earnings beat
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
AMD, Broadcom, CoreWeave stocks mixed on Nvidia Q3 earnings beat
2026-11-19
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/amd-broadcom-tsmc-stocks-rise-on-nvidia-earnings-coreweave-nebius-shares-also-rally-220159436.html
Semiconductor and cloud provider stocks were mixed on Wednesday after AI chip giant Nvidia (NVDA) reported Q3 results that beat Wall Street's expectations. Peers AMD (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) shares rose more than 3%. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM), which manufactures Nvidia's chips, also saw its stock rise modestly.
The semiconductor trade has been volatile since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO last Thursday following reports of extramarital affairs. Wall Street's questions over a succession plan have kept shares of the AI chip heavyweight and the AI trade under pressure.
"I hope that this helps to calm some jitters in the market about the transition," Brian Colello, Morningstar analyst, told Deirdre Bosa Live on Tuesday.
"Seems like business as usual and the forecast is really encouraging as well," he added.
Other areas of the chip trade wavered, including memory chipmaker Micron Technology (MU) and SK Hynix (SKHY), which fell modestly.
Meanwhile, Nvidia-backed CoreWeave (CRWV) fell 4%. Nvidia owns more than 10% of CoreWeave and is a major chip supplier to the AI infrastructure provider. Peer Nebius (NBIS) rose 1%.

item.title: Stable Growth in 2027 Economic Outlook
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Stable Growth in 2027 Economic Outlook
2026-11-18
Por Texto propio
Stable Growth in 2027 Economic Outlook
Key Takeaways
AI infrastructure spending, led by the U.S., should keep global growth steady through 2028, even as energy prices and central bank tightening weigh on some regions.
Morgan Stanley Research expects U.S. AI investment to help global growth hold at 3.3% in 2027 and 3.4% in 2028, down slightly from an estimated 3.5% in 2026.
Rate hikes by developed market central banks should peak in early 2027, and inflation should ease gradually if oil prices stay contained, though core inflation could prove stickier.
Risks run both ways: Even faster growth could result from greater demand momentum or more productivity gains. A shortfall in AI spending or another spike in energy prices would have downside implications for growth.
Solid global economic growth likely will continue in the coming year, helped by capital expenditures for the artificial intelligence buildout and strength in the U.S.
Morgan Stanley Research forecasts the global economy will grow 3.3% in 2027 and 3.4% in 2028, down slightly from an estimated 3.5% in 2026. With developed market central banks hiking interest rates to fight inflation, growth may soften modestly at the start of 2027 and then recover.
“We’re constructive on economic growth in the U.S. and globally,” says Seth Carpenter, Morgan Stanley’s Chief Global Economist and Head of Macro Strategy. Still, the inflation path has become murky. “The energy price shock has reignited headline inflation and raised the prospect of second-round inflation across the globe.”
AI Spending Fuels Strong U.S. Growth
AI infrastructure investment underpins strong U.S. growth, a key driver of the global outlook. Morgan Stanley equity analysts continue to expect hyperscaler capex will climb to about $1.6 trillion in 2027 and almost $1.8 trillion in 2028.
AI-related capital spending and productivity growth should add more than 1 percentage point to U.S. GDP growth as the economy expands by a forecast 2.5% in 2027 and 2.7% in 2028.
“The AI-driven capital expenditures and consumer spending fueled by high-income households are going to keep U.S. growth robust next year,” Carpenter explains. “That strength will help insulate the rest of the world from downside risks.”
Europe, Asia Hold Up as Emerging Markets Slow
Asia’s broader capex super-cycle remains strong, allowing the region to weather higher energy prices and rates. Europe should also see sustained solid growth, with Germany benefiting from further fiscal support, while France lags amid budget constraints. Softer growth at the start of the year will likely be most visible in Japan and the UK, as energy costs weaken demand.
In emerging markets, Morgan Stanley economists see slowing growth. Energy costs are driving stronger inflationary pressures in these economies, prompting policy responses that lean more toward restricting growth. China is an exception, with export-driven growth and subdued inflation.
Rate Hikes Should Be Short-Lived
