Stable Growth in 2027 Economic Outlook

2026-11-18

Por Texto propio

Stable Growth in 2027 Economic Outlook

Key Takeaways

AI infrastructure spending, led by the U.S., should keep global growth steady through 2028, even as energy prices and central bank tightening weigh on some regions.

Morgan Stanley Research expects U.S. AI investment to help global growth hold at 3.3% in 2027 and 3.4% in 2028, down slightly from an estimated 3.5% in 2026.

Rate hikes by developed market central banks should peak in early 2027, and inflation should ease gradually if oil prices stay contained, though core inflation could prove stickier.

Risks run both ways: Even faster growth could result from greater demand momentum or more productivity gains. A shortfall in AI spending or another spike in energy prices would have downside implications for growth.

Solid global economic growth likely will continue in the coming year, helped by capital expenditures for the artificial intelligence buildout and strength in the U.S.

Morgan Stanley Research forecasts the global economy will grow 3.3% in 2027 and 3.4% in 2028, down slightly from an estimated 3.5% in 2026. With developed market central banks hiking interest rates to fight inflation, growth may soften modestly at the start of 2027 and then recover.

“We’re constructive on economic growth in the U.S. and globally,” says Seth Carpenter, Morgan Stanley’s Chief Global Economist and Head of Macro Strategy. Still, the inflation path has become murky. “The energy price shock has reignited headline inflation and raised the prospect of second-round inflation across the globe.”

AI Spending Fuels Strong U.S. Growth

AI infrastructure investment underpins strong U.S. growth, a key driver of the global outlook. Morgan Stanley equity analysts continue to expect hyperscaler capex will climb to about $1.6 trillion in 2027 and almost $1.8 trillion in 2028.

AI-related capital spending and productivity growth should add more than 1 percentage point to U.S. GDP growth as the economy expands by a forecast 2.5% in 2027 and 2.7% in 2028.

“The AI-driven capital expenditures and consumer spending fueled by high-income households are going to keep U.S. growth robust next year,” Carpenter explains. “That strength will help insulate the rest of the world from downside risks.”

Europe, Asia Hold Up as Emerging Markets Slow

Asia’s broader capex super-cycle remains strong, allowing the region to weather higher energy prices and rates. Europe should also see sustained solid growth, with Germany benefiting from further fiscal support, while France lags amid budget constraints. Softer growth at the start of the year will likely be most visible in Japan and the UK, as energy costs weaken demand.

In emerging markets, Morgan Stanley economists see slowing growth. Energy costs are driving stronger inflationary pressures in these economies, prompting policy responses that lean more toward restricting growth. China is an exception, with export-driven growth and subdued inflation.

Rate Hikes Should Be Short-Lived

Developed market central banks have raised rates to contain the inflation set off by the energy price shock. From here, the current interest-rate hiking cycle should be relatively short-lived.

Morgan Stanley Research economists expect the Federal Reserve to raise the U.S. benchmark rate to a peak of 4.25%–4.50% in the first quarter of 2027, up from the current 3.75%–4.00%. They see the European Central Bank hiking rates to 3.0%, up from 2.5% today, and the Bank of Japan to 1.75%, up from 1.25%. The Bank of England is also likely to hike. They expect a modest rate cutting cycle in 2028.

“Even central banks that are not hiking are keeping policy tighter than might otherwise have been expected,” Carpenter says.

item.title: Markets in 2027- Stocks Take the Lead
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Markets in 2027- Stocks Take the Lead
2026-11-18
Por Texto propio
Markets in 2027: Stocks Take the Lead
Key Takeaways
Morgan Stanley Research forecasts the S&P 500 Index will rise about 15% from mid-November levels to reach 8,700 in 12 months.
Elevated borrowing costs favor companies with strong balance sheets, durable profit margins and solid cash generation.
Strategists maintain neutral allocations to core fixed income and corporate credit, while highlighting UK and German government bonds and favoring investment-grade debt.
The U.S. dollar could strengthen modestly, while oil prices could ease toward $75 a barrel by late 2027. Gold remains the top commodity pick.
Resilient economic growth, healthy corporate earnings and abundant credit should carry into 2027, supported by an intact AI investment cycle. Several major unknowns for investors seem to be in the past.
That combination should favor risk assets in 2027, according to Morgan Stanley Research’s 2027 Global Investment Outlook. The Firm’s strategists recommend a maximum overweight allocation to equities and neutral allocations to core fixed income and corporate credit, while downgrading commodities and cash to underweight.
“The biggest change since our midyear outlook is how much more attractive risk has become,” says Serena Tang, Morgan Stanley’s Chief Cross-Asset Strategist. “Stocks and corporate bonds have cheapened even as expectations for AI investment have risen. And of course, we’re heading into 2027 with more clarity on two big unknowns—the U.S. midterm elections are behind us and markets better understand the Federal Reserve’s reaction function.”
An intact AI infrastructure investment cycle is central to this investment thesis. Morgan Stanley Research maintains its forecast that the total AI hyperscaler and related capital expenditure will be $1.7 trillion in 2027 and $1.8 trillion in 2028. Beyond the scale of spending, investors will increasingly look for evidence that companies are generating revenue and realizing benefits from AI adoption.
However, risks cannot be overlooked. Central banks could raise interest rates even more in response to strong growth and persistent inflation. Conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine could continue to drive volatility in energy markets, while Europe faces a wave of elections in 2027 and tariff impacts persist.
“Over the last two years, risk assets and the broader economy have proven more resilient than many had expected when faced with these same risks,” Tang says. “We believe they can be resilient again in the face of these unknowns. But policy uncertainty globally could produce very different outcomes across markets. So, timing and diversification will be critical.”
Taking Risk While Favoring Quality
While investors should be more open to risk assets, they should also favor quality.
“Resilient economic growth lifts most boats, but not all equally: Funding costs remain elevated and borrowing needs at highs,” says Vishwanath Tirupattur, Chief Fixed Income Strategist and Director of Quantitative Research at Morgan Stanley.
High-quality hyperscalers have access to multiple financing channels, but borrowers with high debt levels may struggle to refinance. Within U.S. equities, Morgan Stanley strategists favor companies with strong balance sheets, durable margins and solid cash generation.
The recommendation on U.S. Treasuries is neutral alongside the overweight allocation to equities. Government bonds provided a buffer during the recent technology stock sell-off and remain a useful source of portfolio diversification.
“Embrace risk, but all the more reason to embrace quality too,” Tirupattur says.
Stocks: AI Spending and Earnings Support the Outlook
Higher AI investment should continue to support economic growth and corporate earnings in the U.S. and globally. Earnings per share are likely to grow more than 10% in 2027 in the U.S., Japan and emerging markets.

item.title: Timothee Chalamet Came Over for Lunch-and a Cover Story
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Timothee Chalamet Came Over for Lunch-and a Cover Story
2026-11-18
Por Texto propio
Vanity Fair editor Mark Guiducci welcomes the actor into his home—and readers to the 2026 Holiday Issue.
BY MARK GUIDUCCI
PHOTOGRAPHS BY AIDAN ZAMIRI
NOVEMBER 17, 2026
The history of actors appearing in *Vanity Fair* goes back about as far as the movies themselves. Making a studio-orchestrated, Edward Steichen—captured debut in the pages of this magazine was a milestone in the careers of *Gary Cooper*, *Gloria Swanson*, *Anna May Wong*, and dozens of others, many of whom never made it to Technicolor.
On more than one occasion, the idea of *Timothée Chalamet* as the *last* male movie star has been a debate here at the office, usually ending in uneasy agreement: He is one of very few left, maybe the only one of his generation. He is in the tradition of *Marlon Brando* and *Leonardo DiCaprio* in that his knowability runs inverse to his fame. Like other endangered species, his extreme rarity makes him celebrated and isolated in equal measure. And with each of these stars, one rule usually holds true: The bigger they get, the less they open their mouth.
All of which is why we are thrilled to have Chalamet on our cover as he sets out to open the final, breathtaking installment of *Denis Villeneuve's Dune trilogy*. He and our team, led by photographer Aidan Zamiri, fashion editor Taylor McNeill (with whom I was an assistant at this magazine in 2010), and *VF* global creative director Jennifer Pastore, trekked to Iceland for a multiday shoot to capture his cover story “*A Star on Planet Earth*. ” Everyone involved—including and especially Timothée—approached it more like a film, or maybe a music video, than a typical cover, and there is a spiritual quality that runs throughout the pictures. “I love that being on the edge of a cliff in Iceland,” Timothée tells me, “you get the same feeling as being in Grand Central.”
Timothée also had the idea that I write the cover story myself, and while I was reluctant, I eventually thought, Why not mix it up? He came over to my apartment in early October for a conversation about *Dune*; his career; the careers of other actors, musicians, and painters; and especially the careers of the *New York Knicks*. I took away from our meeting that he may be a movie star, sure, but he approaches everything as an artist. The writing process is a humbling one, though—okay, it's agony—and since filing the cover story, I have come to believe that every editor really should write a feature now and again to make us more understanding of our writers. Perhaps once a year. Consider it a new rule at *Vanity Fair*.
Timothée and I were both reading Kevin Roose's *The AGI Chronicles* when we met up, and he pointed out that the first several chapters of the book might as well have been the source material for *Artificial*, *Luca Guadagnino's new film starring Andrew Garfield* and Yura Borisov. The film presents a villain origin story of OpenAI's cofounders, particularly *CEO Sam Altman*. It is the natural inheritor to David Fincher and Aaron Sorkin's 2010 film, *The Social Network*, which similarly helped answer the how-did-we-get-here question for another quite recent era of technology.
In case you missed it, Altman was recently on the cover of *Vanity Fair*, sitting atop our revived New Establishment list. It inspired a torrent of furious reader feedback, including a few death threats. I understand that those messages were rooted in genuine fear of this technology and ire toward its Dr. Frankenstein founders (and me, by extension, for covering them). But reporting on the powerful—whether power is granted by elections or equities or zettaflops of compute—has always been the mandate of this magazine and will continue to be. We'll keep the movie stars too.
COVER STORY
A Star on Planet Earth
From the deserts of Arrakis to the lonely fjords of Iceland, Timothée Chalamet doesn't do anything halfway. Mark Guiducci invites a celebri

item.title: Nvidia posts Q3 beat
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Nvidia posts Q3 beat
2026-11-18
Por Texto propio
Nvidia posts Q3 beat as revenue rose 103% YOY to $115.8B, board says it will not reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
By Daniel Howley
Nvidia (NVDA) reported its Q3 results after the bell Tuesday, beating Wall Street's expectations on the top and bottom lines and offering a better-than-anticipated Q4 outlook. The company also announced a $150 billion stock buyback. Nvidia stock rose on the news.
For the fourth quarter, Nvidia expects revenue between $127.4 billion and $132.6 billion. Analysts were anticipating $125.25 billion

item.title: US 10-Year Yield Set for Historic Run Above 5% on Fed Rate Cycle
item.author: Michael MacKenzie
item.description:
US 10-Year Yield Set for Historic Run Above 5% on Fed Rate Cycle
2026-11-18
Por Michael MacKenzie
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/us-10-yield-set-historic-151500006.html
(Bloomberg) -- The US's 10-year Treasury yield is nearing its longest run above 5% in almost two decades as investors position for the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates more amid stubbornly elevated inflation.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The benchmark for borrowing costs in the world's largest economy is on pace to hold above 5% for the 27th day this year, putting 2026 within striking distance of the 29 such closes recorded in 2007. It was about one basis point higher at 5.14% after US retail sales growth moderated in October.
Upward pressure on yields comes after hotter-than-expected October inflation forced Fed policymakers to begin considering a more aggressively tightening of monetary policy than previously expected.
Traders are now fully pricing a quarter-point rate increase at the central bank's Dec. 9 meeting and see more than 80 basis points of tightening by September 2027, compared with roughly 50 basis points before last week.
Yields back over 5% reflect "risk premium due to uncertainty about the Fed," said Priya Misra, portfolio manager at JPMorgan Asset Management.
The resilient economy and lots of bond sales, from the US government as well as companies looking to invest in AI are other reasons for yields staying above 5%, she said.
The 10-year is a benchmark for the US economy as it helps set the cost of home mortgages, credit cards and business loans. Back in 2007, the 10-year yield climbed above 5% in June and peaked at 5.32% as the Fed kept rates at 5.25% they first reached in July 2006.
That set the stage for elevated rates to weigh on the housing sector, which prompted the central bank to cut rates in September.
For Ian Lyngen, head of US rate strategy at BMO Capital Markets, the current elevated yields are already a cause for concern.
"The impact on the real estate market has been to effectively freeze activity," he said. That's "a foreseeable outcome given the fact that 30-year mortgages have remained above 7% since mid-September."
The trajectory of Treasury yields this year, while not in a straight line, has generally followed an upward path, with the 10-year's rising from under 4% when President Donald Trump launched his war on Iran in late February, disrupting the supply of Middle Eastern oil and gas.

item.title: Google Buys AI Scheduling Tool Howie in Latest Agents Push
item.author: Natalie Lung
item.description:
Google Buys AI Scheduling Tool Howie in Latest Agents Push
2026-11-18
Por Natalie Lung
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/google-buys-ai-scheduling-tool-161136571.html
(Bloomberg) -- Alphabet Inc.'s Google has bought Howie, an artificial intelligence-powered scheduling and calendar management tool, the tech giant's latest move to win over consumers with AI agents.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Google's experimental arm, Google Labs, announced the purchase Monday in an X post, without disclosing terms. Howie, whose tool lets users loop the AI agent into emails as they would a human secretary, was valued at $14 million in 2024, according to PitchBook data.
"We can't wait to learn from them as we build the next generation of intuitive AI tools together for small businesses," Google Labs said in the post.
Tech and AI companies have been intensely focused on developing AI agents that can do things on behalf of the user, an advancement beyond question-and-answer chatbots. In May, Google released Gemini Spark, a 24/7 agent that proactively completes digital tasks such as scan an inbox for emails, organize files or build a spreadsheet. That market is growing increasingly crowded, with offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic PBC, Meta Platforms Inc. and Elon Musk's xAI.
Petersmith and Google Labs did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the deal terms, or whether Howie will eventually be integrated into Google apps and services.
Google Labs has previously acquired AI tools built on Google technology. In February, it bought ProducerAI, a music generation platform that uses Google DeepMind's Lyria model.
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Goldman Sachs is looking for a big year for stocks in 2027
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Goldman Sachs is looking for a big year for stocks in 2027
2026-11-18
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/goldman-sachs-is-looking-for-a-big-year-for-stocks-in-2027-142151047.html
Goldman Sachs is backing up the truck on stocks for 2027.
"We forecast an S&P 500 total return of 18% to a year-end 2027 level of 8,700, including a dividend yield of 1%," Goldman Sachs strategist Ben Snider wrote on Tuesday.
The S&P 500 (^GSPC) closed on Monday at 7,416.59 and is within arm's reach of double-digit gains for 2026.
Snider added, "Earnings should grow by a robust 11% in 2027, or 18% excluding mega-cap tech "other income" from private investment stakes. However, that is a step down from the roughly 30% growth rate in 2026, and growth will likely slow further in 2028."
This is breaking news. Check back for updates.

item.title: Consumer staples stocks benefiting from a powerful rotation as tech gets slammed
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Consumer staples stocks benefiting from a powerful rotation as tech gets slammed
2026-11-18
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/consumer-staples-stocks-benefiting-from-a-powerful-rotation-as-tech-gets-slammed-173929452.html
Investors continue to find comfort in boring consumer staples stocks as growth expectations for the tech giants driving the AI boom come under closer scrutiny.
The S&P 500 (^GSPC) tech sector's (XLK) forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is currently 17.2 times, its lowest level since 2020, according to data crunched by Duality Research. The S&P 500's consumer staples (XLP) sector forward P/E ratio of 24.2 times is at the highest level since 1999.
The S&P 500 consumer staples and tech sectors are up 18.7% and 12.7%, respectively, on the year.
"Is staples the actual bubble here? The sector's years to date gains are almost entirely attributable to multiple expansion," Duality Research noted.
Investors are rotating aggressively into consumer staples stocks to seek shelter from the sharp sell-off in high-flying technology and artificial intelligence shares.
Persistent inflation and elevated borrowing costs are squeezing household budgets, pushing shoppers to prioritize everyday necessities over discretionary upgrades.
Companies like Costco (COST), Procter & Gamble (PG), and Coca-Cola (KO) sell essential goods, and their cash flows and pricing power remain resilient during economic slowdowns. Additionally, these mature businesses offer reliable dividend yields that attract capital during periods of broader market volatility.
Read more: How to protect your money during turmoil, stock market volatility
As institutional funds rebalance away from crowded momentum trades, staples have emerged as a safe-haven trade.
You can see it in the tape: P&G shares are up 9% over the past month, Coca-Cola is trading near a record high, and even struggling Campbell's (CPB) has seen its stock climb 20% in the past month.
Despite higher prices for consumer goods, consumers haven't retrenched — which has also helped sentiment on staples.
"The US consumer is remarkably resilient," P&G CFO Andre Schulten told Yahoo Finance in late October.
Schulten said the business is being powered by higher-income households, while the lower end is being more cautious.

item.title: Fed needs to prepare for bond-market intervention during calm times, Hammack says
item.author: Reuters
item.description:
Fed needs to prepare for bond-market intervention during calm times, Hammack says
2026-11-18
Por Reuters
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/fed-needs-prepare-bond-market-143914934.html
Nov 17 (Reuters) - The US central bank should start preparing principles now for potential temporary and targeted interventions in the Treasury market in times of market stress that threatens to bleed over into the economy, Cleveland Federal Reserve President Beth Hammack said on Tuesday.
It is time to learn from two recent market upheavals — in March 2020 at the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic and in April 2025 after the announcement of an aggressive tariff regime by President Donald Trump — with the goal of preventing the next one, Hammack said in remarks prepared for an event at the Brookings Institution in Washington.
Hammack did not address the economic or monetary policy outlook in her prepared remarks.
"When stress hits, there may be very little time to decide what principles to operate under or how to communicate them," Hammack said. "It is better to identify the exit routes when you first enter the building than it is to draw up an evacuation plan as the building is filling with smoke."
The Fed needs a clear understanding of when it will and will not intervene, she said.
In cases where officials assess that market dysfunction could spill into the economy and Fed actions could resolve the issue, "intervention should be considered," Hammack said. But "when poor liquidity conditions in volatile markets reflect fundamentals, it is not a problem the Fed can or should try to solve," she added.
Hammack said she supports enhancements to the Fed's Standing Repo Facility, which provides liquidity to financial institutions in exchange for Treasuries. In its current form, it might not have been sufficient to address the market dislocations witnessed at the start of the pandemic, she said.
"I doubt repos would have been enough in 2020," Hammack said. "Thus, it may make sense to consider Treasury purchases if repo operations prove insufficient."
In instances where outright Treasury purchases may be required, the Fed should approach them with clear communication distinguishing the action from any monetary policy actions and should also have an exit plan, she said.
"The presumption should be that the action is temporary and targeted, ideally with an exit strategy built in from the start," Hammack said.
Hammack's comments on the Fed's market stabilization role largely dovetail with remarks last week from Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan.
(Reporting by Dan Burns; Editing by Paul Simao)

Hammack said she supports enhancements to the Fed's Standing Repo Facility, which provides liquidity to financial institutions in exchange for Treasuries. In its current form, it might not have been sufficient to address the market dislocations witnessed at the start of the pandemic, she said.
"I doubt repos would have been enough in 2020," Hammack said. "Thus, it may make sense to consider Treasury purchases if repo operations prove insufficient."
In instances where outright Treasury purchases may be required, the Fed should approach them with clear communication distinguishing the action from any monetary policy actions and should also have an exit plan, she said.
"The presumption should be that the action is temporary and targeted, ideally with an exit strategy built in from the start," Hammack said.
Hammack's comments on the Fed's market stabilization role largely dovetail with remarks last week from Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan.
(Reporting by Dan Burns; Editing by Paul Simao)

A new era of disruptive cyber outages is making the nonstop data breaches of just a few years ago seem quaint.
The recent cascade of breaks and digital dislocations feels like a preview to a more chaotic and disordered world, where everything is connected but also vulnerable and exploitable. AI is accelerating innovation, but it's also supercharging the capabilities of bad actors and increasing the blast radius for outages and overall online messiness.
Here's a brief rundown of what we've seen over the past week.

For about 36 hours, much of corporate America's productivity suite went offline. Microsoft's signature platforms, including Outlook and Teams, stopped working. More than 70 countries and territories experienced the outage, hampering millions of users.
"This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents," Microsoft explained. "The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change."
National flight grounding and FAA ATC outage — Nov. 13
The Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop for more than four hours, unleashing a wave of delays and cancellations across the country. Outdated air traffic communications equipment and copper cable upgrades were to blame.
While the stoppage lasted a handful of hours, its impacts rippled across air travel for several days as airlines scrambled to rebook passengers and get aircraft and crew back in place. The incident has become a political headache for the Trump administration and highlighted the nation's aging telecommunications infrastructure and its vulnerabilities.
JPMorgan (and others) banking outage — Nov. 16
Thousands of customers reported problems with their online banking services at several major institutions, tied back to a technical issue at JPMorgan Chase.
JPMorgan Chase said in a statement that it "has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems," adding that "there is no evidence this is cyber-related."
The disruption, coming on the heels of the other major outages, sparked concerns that the events were connected, and that hackers were to blame.
Users who made transactions involving Chase and other banks made it appear that the outage was systemic, but Chase said its banking platform was responsible.
In other cases, security researchers identified malicious code in online tools used by nearly 200 organizations, including reportedly Zoom, HSBC, and Equifax.

Neither CNN nor the NSA elaborated on the causes, but said there was currently no evidence of a cyberattack.

item.title: Home Depot taps Richard McPhail as new CEO, reports Q3 earnings beat
item.author: Brooke DiPalma
item.description:
Home Depot taps Richard McPhail as new CEO, reports Q3 earnings beat
2026-11-18
Por Brooke DiPalma
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/home-depot-taps-richard-mcphail-as-new-ceo-reports-q3-earnings-beat-111428412.html
Home Depot (HD) beat Wall Street's metrics across the board in the third quarter and adjusted its full-year outlook amid a shake-up in its C-suite leadership.
The company announced that Richard McPhail, who joined the company in 2005 and currently serves as CFO, will become CEO on Nov. 23. Current CEO Ted Decker has returned from temporary medical leave and will continue to serve as chair of the board, Home Depot said.
Decker, who became CEO in 2022, told investors on its earnings call that he is "grateful for the support" he received, and that "The Board and I have agreed that now is the right time to move to the next phase of our succession plan."
Jordan Broggi, a 13-year veteran of Home Depot, will take the CFO role, while senior executive vice president Ann-Marie Campbell was promoted to president and COO.
In the third quarter, revenue grew by nearly 5% to $43.4 billion, above the $42.8 billion analysts forecast, per Bloomberg estimates. Adjusted earnings per share grew 3% to $3.86, more than the $3.85 predicted.
"Results in the third quarter exceeded our expectations," incoming CEO McPhail said in the release. "Our associates' strong engagement and exceptional execution, combined with our continued investments across the business, enabled us to grow market share in a dynamic environment."
Home Depot stock declined slightly in premarket trading following the announcement.
Same-store sales increased 2.2%, more than the roughly 1.7% expected. US same-store sales also jumped 2.2%, above the 1.5% expected, but a sluggish housing environment persists, as US homebuilder confidence fell to its lowest level in more than 14 years.
The company said the average ticket size increased by 3% due to a mix of inflation and some customers trading up to new and innovative products. But customers had fewer visits to Home Depot stores.
Transactions for big ticket items above $1,000 increased by 4.5% compared to Q3 last year.
Home Depot said it saw strength in its power department, which saw double-digit growth, as well as in storage, plumbing, and electrical, which grew by mid-single-digit percentages.
These results come as the average 30-year fixed-rate remains above 7%.
The company adjusted its 2026 forecast. It now expects total sales to grow by 4.5%, at the high end of its previously expected range for the year, and expects its same-store sales growth outlook to be up 1.4%, toward the higher end of its previously expected range of flat to up 2%.
McPhail said that "a rising interest rate environment puts pressure on our customer and our business" and its guidance reflects that.
Lowe's (LOW) is expected to post a same-store sales increase of 0.4% when it reports quarterly results on Wednesday.
Brooke DiPalma is a reporter for Yahoo Finance. Follow her on X at @BrookeDiPalma or email her at bdipalma@yahoofinance.com.

item.title: JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum to step down as Jamie Dimon's succession plans take shape
item.author: David Hollerith
item.description:
JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum to step down as Jamie Dimon's succession plans take shape
2026-11-18
Por David Hollerith
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/jpmorgan-cfo-jeremy-barnum-to-step-down-as-jamie-dimons-succession-plans-take-shape-153110270.html
JPMorgan Chase (JPM) said Tuesday that longtime CFO Jeremy Barnum will step down next year in the latest change among the top ranks of the country's largest bank as it prepares for CEO Jamie Dimon's eventual succession.
Barnum, who has served as the bank's CFO since 2021, will be succeeded by Bregje de Best, CFO of JPMorgan's commercial and investment bank, after the company's first quarter earnings in April, according to a JPMorgan filing.
Barnum will become vice chair, remaining with the bank until early 2028, JPMorgan said. Dimon added in a press release statement that Barnum had requested the transition after six years in the role.
That tenure is slightly above average for a CFO at a large US company, according to a 2025 study by executive search firm Spencer Stuart, which found CFOs at S&P 500 companies had served an average of 4.8 years in their positions.
The announcement comes less than a week after Allison Beer, JPMorgan's head of credit card and connected commerce, informed colleagues that she was leaving to pursue another opportunity, according to an internal JPMorgan memo.
It also follows a broader leadership shake-up of Dimon's top lieutenants earlier this year when JPMorgan announced the retirement of Marianne Lake, the former head of its sprawling consumer bank and previously a leading candidate to succeed Dimon.
The announcement of Lake's departure also came as JPMorgan said it was elevating executives Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh to the role of co-president, signaling their leads to eventually take the reins from Dimon, who was expected to stay for three more years as CEO, according to an executive familiar with the matter who spoke to Yahoo Finance at the time.
Barnum's planned transition and Lake's retirement are part of a broader effort to prepare JPMorgan's next generation of leadership, according to a person familiar with the bank's succession planning.
The person characterized Beer's departure as separate, saying the credit card executive was seeking a broader leadership role than her current responsibilities at the bank.
De Best, 43, joined JPMorgan in 2006 and has held senior positions across investment banking, markets and corporate banking. She will also join the firm's operating committee when she assumes the CFO role.
Morgan Stanley analyst Manan Gosalia said Tuesday his team "do[es] not expect the CFO transition itself to have any impact on JPM's strategy or preliminary 2027 outlook."
RBC Capital Markets analyst Gerard Cassidy also told clients Tuesday, in reaction to Barnum's departure, that senior management shake-ups are not unusual at JPMorgan.
"We expect JPM's deep management bench will continue to enable the company to effectively manage through senior executive realignment," Cassidy said.
Follow David Hollerith on X @DsHollers.

item.title: New York Fed’s Williams rules out jumbo rate hike for December
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
New York Fed’s Williams rules out jumbo rate hike for December
2026-11-18
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/new-york-feds-williams-rules-out-jumbo-rate-hike-for-december-205144565.html
New York Federal Reserve president John Williams poured cold water on the central bank making a jumbo 50-basis-point interest rate hike next month but noted that the Fed does have to get inflation down.
"I don't think the situation calls for dramatic action," Williams said during a Q&A with Axios in New York.
Williams acknowledged that the data is sending a "pretty clear signal."
"We still have our work to do to make sure that we bring inflation back down to 2% in a timely way and in a sustained manner," he said.
Read more: How the Fed rate decision affects your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments
Williams' comments come as the latest inflation data shows price growth that is surprisingly higher than expected. The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October, compared with expectations of 0.3%, marking a slight cooldown from September's 0.6% gain. "Core" inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.3%, compared with expectations of 0.2% and unchanged from September.
A reading of the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge showed prices heated up in September, with the core Personal Consumption Expenditures index rising 3.1%, up a tenth of a percentage point from 3% in August.
Markets have been weighing a larger rate hike ever since inflation readings came in hot. Fed governor Chris Waller said ahead of the CPI report that if consumer prices were higher than expected, he'd consider a move of 50 basis points.
After Williams spoke on Tuesday, investors still saw a 98% chance the Fed hikes by 25 basis points in December.
Williams wouldn't characterize inflation as broadening, but acknowledged a continuation of higher price increases on imported goods where tariffs are in place and energy prices that are being passed on. He also pointed to AI investments causing certain prices, such as semiconductors, to rise. Williams identified AI as the most likely "persistent" factor of inflation.
How many rate hikes and at what pace the Fed must implement them will depend on what's happening in AI, Williams said. He noted that a lot of strength in the economy is coming from AI, and consumer spending is being boosted by a strong stock market.
"If those continue, I think that that's a factor that will argue that we may need to raise rates more at the same time those factors have been pushing inflation up. But there's just a great deal of uncertainty," he said.
item.content:encoded:
New York Fed’s Williams rules out jumbo rate hike for December

2026-11-18

Por Jennifer Schonberger

https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/new-york-feds-williams-rules-out-jumbo-rate-hike-for-december-205144565.html

New York Federal Reserve president John Williams poured cold water on the central bank making a jumbo 50-basis-point interest rate hike next month but noted that the Fed does have to get inflation down.

"I don't think the situation calls for dramatic action," Williams said during a Q&A with Axios in New York.

Williams acknowledged that the data is sending a "pretty clear signal."

"We still have our work to do to make sure that we bring inflation back down to 2% in a timely way and in a sustained manner," he said.

Read more: How the Fed rate decision affects your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments

Williams' comments come as the latest inflation data shows price growth that is surprisingly higher than expected. The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October, compared with expectations of 0.3%, marking a slight cooldown from September's 0.6% gain. "Core" inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.3%, compared with expectations of 0.2% and unchanged from September.

A reading of the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge showed prices heated up in September, with the core Personal Consumption Expenditures index rising 3.1%, up a tenth of a percentage point from 3% in August.

Markets have been weighing a larger rate hike ever since inflation readings came in hot. Fed governor Chris Waller said ahead of the CPI report that if consumer prices were higher than expected, he'd consider a move of 50 basis points.

After Williams spoke on Tuesday, investors still saw a 98% chance the Fed hikes by 25 basis points in December.

Williams wouldn't characterize inflation as broadening, but acknowledged a continuation of higher price increases on imported goods where tariffs are in place and energy prices that are being passed on. He also pointed to AI investments causing certain prices, such as semiconductors, to rise. Williams identified AI as the most likely "persistent" factor of inflation.

How many rate hikes and at what pace the Fed must implement them will depend on what's happening in AI, Williams said. He noted that a lot of strength in the economy is coming from AI, and consumer spending is being boosted by a strong stock market.

"If those continue, I think that that's a factor that will argue that we may need to raise rates more at the same time those factors have been pushing inflation up. But there's just a great deal of uncertainty," he said.

item.title: Treasuries Rise as Risk-Averse Investors Dump Stocks, Buy Bonds
item.author: Elizabeth Stanton; Victor Swezey
item.description:
Treasuries Rise as Risk-Averse Investors Dump Stocks, Buy Bonds
2026-11-18
Por Elizabeth Stanton; Victor Swezey
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/articles/treasuries-rise-risk-averse-investors-162624439.html
(Bloomberg) -- Treasuries gained as investors, alarmed by the latest in a series of technology breakdowns over the past week, flocked to US government bonds as a haven from stocks.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The rally trimmed yields across maturities by as much as four to five basis points. They had risen earlier in the session after October retail sales data were stronger than anticipated, backing expectations for additional Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes.
The bond rally coincided with US equity market benchmarks tumbling to session lows, led by large technology company shares. The S&P 500 Index fell as much as 1.7%, the Nasdaq 100 Index 2.3% to the lowest level since April, in the minutes after CNN reported that a National Security Agency network had gone down, the latest in a series of breakdowns that have crippled airlines and financial services companies over the past week.
"Fear of the unknown seems to be dominating rate space near term," said David Robin, an interest-rate strategist at TJM Institutional Services LLC. "The bursting of the AI bubble, coupled with the difficult-to-quantify-or-understand headline risk of technology breakdowns and cyber attacks, is causing a flight to safety."
It's aggravated, Robin said, by uncertainty regarding what the Fed will do on Dec. 9 and the paucity of influential economic data in the next two weeks. Short-term interest-rate contracts fully price in a quarter-point interest rate hike as well as an outside chance of a half-point increase.
"There really wasn't anything to explain the hit to equities and the bid to Treasuries beyond the NSA headlines," said Izaac Brook, US rates strategist at RBC Capital Markets. "This is all just catalyst for chopping around in the range we carved out after payrolls, inflation data and Fedspeak."
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Microsoft's AI pitch at Ignite: Cheaper models as business 'token spend is going through the roof'
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Microsoft's AI pitch at Ignite: Cheaper models as business 'token spend is going through the roof'
2026-11-18
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/microsoft-ignite-focuses-on-ai-models-for-specific-tasks-lowering-costs-for-enterprise-203433266.html
Microsoft (MSFT) announced a slew of AI improvements at its Ignite conference on Tuesday. One message stood out: The tech giant is focused on making AI cheaper for businesses by offering specialized models for specific tasks. In some cases, the tasks that would've taken the company weeks were performed in minutes.
Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman said he is hearing time and again from enterprises that "token spend is going through the roof."
"Our commitment is to give you the very best price performance out there, so that you can really scale your agents," Suleyman said. "And we also know that you want models that feel truly yours."
During the conference, executives highlighted Microsoft IQ, a new platform designed to help businesses organize and share employees' knowledge, expertise, and tools. The idea is to help AI systems learn how a company works and build on that knowledge over time.
CEO Satya Nadella highlighted the launch of new AI models for coding, cybersecurity, and decision making. The company's flagship coding model, MAI Code 2, is designed to handle complex, time-consuming programming tasks, work across multiple files, and understand entire software projects.
Nadella also underscored Copilot Fusion, which orchestrates "multiple models to deliver frontier-level results at significantly lower costs."
Microsoft highlighted a feature that selects the right model for the task, making it easier to maximize output quality while managing the cost of each request.
Nadella kicked off the conference by acknowledging last week's outage, which spanned regions.
"We know the trust you place in our services and take that responsibility very seriously, and in that context, I know we have work to do," Nadella said.
"We are committed to ensuring that we learn and we continuously improve," he added.

item.title: Disney holds the line on park pricing as screen-weary consumers seek 'real experiences'
item.author: Brooke DiPalma
item.description:
Disney holds the line on park pricing as screen-weary consumers seek 'real experiences'
2026-11-18
Por Brooke DiPalma
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/disney-holds-the-line-on-park-pricing-as-screen-weary-consumers-seek-real-experiences-165741949.html
Disney doesn't plan to change its park pricing anytime soon, as its experiences segment, including both parks and cruises, hit a record revenue last quarter.
"We feel very good about the current trends," CEO Josh D'Amaro said, adding that bookings for the first quarter in 2027 are higher compared to 2026.
"It's more than about just ticket price," D'Amaro said. "Consumers want real experiences now … we're seeing that accelerate. People today are spending so much of their lives on screens. They're just looking for time to connect with each other in the real world … Disney parks [are] one of the few places that you can actually do that."
Disney saw a record number of guests at its parks last quarter, the company said. D'Amaro added that Disney has more projects underway around the world than "any other point in history."
A lot of Disney's focus is on its Orlando resort, especially on Monstropolis at Disney's Hollywood Studios, Lake Shore Lodge, and Tropical Americas in Animal Kingdom. Disney also has plans to double the size of the Avengers Campus at Disneyland California by 2028.
NerdWallet found that a seven-night trip to Disney with a family of four could easily top $6,000 — and that's for a "frugal traveler."
Read more: Best credit cards for Disney vacations (2026)
In the most recent quarter, Disney reported an 11% increase in global guests visiting its parks and experiences, led by Disneyland Paris. Disney also increased capacity for its Disney Cruise Line following the launches of the Disney Adventure and Disney Destiny cruise ships.
Customers spent more at Disney parks too. Average spending per customer on admissions, food, and merchandise in US parks rose 4%, more than the expected 3.6% in the US. Internationally, sales at Disneyland Paris offset weakness in Hong Kong and Shanghai parks.
While the company is largely holding firm on prices, it is offering promotions and programs for Florida residents, its annual passholders, and Disney+ subscribers.
Disney is also exploring offering a free ad-supported version of its Disney+ streaming service.
"We are exploring a free product, and I think it will be more price-sensitive consumer and bring in new Disney+ subscribers," D'Amaro told investors. "It's going to give us more ad inventory to … offer a key retention tool that, quite frankly, we currently don't have."
A bundle deal for Disney+ and Hulu with ads currently costs $11.99 a month. Without ads, it costs $19.99 a month, and you're able to download movies and series. That could change soon.

item.title: There's 'no difference' between buying Anthropic's IPO and Amazon's IPO: Kevin O'Leary
item.author: Paige Oamek
item.description:
There's 'no difference' between buying Anthropic's IPO and Amazon's IPO: Kevin O'Leary
2026-11-18
Por Paige Oamek
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/theres-no-difference-between-buying-anthropics-ipo-and-amazons-ipo-kevin-oleary-190707549.html
As Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) prepares to begin trading under the ticker ANT on Thursday, Nov. 19, business leaders are weighing in on the historically large initial public offering (IPO).
"There's no difference in investing in Anthropic on the IPO than Amazon on its IPO," "Shark Tank" host and O'Leary Ventures chair Kevin O'Leary said on Sozzi Unleashed. "There was tremendous volatility. It made zero money. But look at the platform it ultimately built. That's what you're betting on in the Anthropic deal."
Sitting down with Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi, O'Leary said the past few years haven't been great for buying IPOs, but he believes Anthropic may be a unique way to bet on artificial intelligence.
Anthropic said it expects to sell 825 million shares priced between $70 and $78 each. That would give the company a market valuation of between $1.3 trillion and $1.45 trillion — putting it near SpaceX's (SPCX) IPO valuation of $1.77 trillion, which was the largest ever.
Read more: Everything you need to know ahead of Anthropic's IPO
"It may be the most hyped IPO ever," O'Leary said. "This IPO is the anchor to the entire AI or SI trade, whatever you want to call it."
What about the fact that Anthropic may not turn a profit until 2030? Though Anthropic's operating losses have improved, they still total $1.3 billion for the first nine months of the year. The company also noted in its amended IPO filing that it plans to spend nearly $900 billion on computing and data centers, with $70 billion of that total coming due within a year.
O'Leary said Anthropic's profitability is the wrong lens right now. Buying in is a bet on AI's role across all 11 sectors of the economy, and he sees evidence of productivity and margin gains so far. That has helped markets remain near all-time highs despite tariffs, wars, and high energy prices.
These remarks follow O'Leary's comments last month, when the businessman called Anthropic "a hot trade."
"I expect it to be liquid from day one, and that changes the opportunity," he wrote in October.

The company also noted in its amended IPO filing that it plans to spend nearly $900 billion on computing and data centers, with $70 billion of that total coming due within a year.
O'Leary said Anthropic's profitability is the wrong lens right now. Buying in is a bet on AI's role across all 11 sectors of the economy, and he sees evidence of productivity and margin gains so far. That has helped markets remain near all-time highs despite tariffs, wars, and high energy prices.
These remarks follow O'Leary's comments last month, when the businessman called Anthropic "a hot trade."
"I expect it to be liquid from day one, and that changes the opportunity," he wrote in October.

item.title: Disney stock rises after Q4 earnings beat estimates, company sets $3 billion cost savings target
item.author: Brooke DiPalma
item.description:
Disney stock rises after Q4 earnings beat estimates, company sets $3 billion cost savings target
2026-11-18
Por Brooke DiPalma
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/disney-stock-rises-after-q4-earnings-beat-estimates-company-sets-3-billion-cost-savings-target-152507234.html
Disney's (DIS) fourth quarter earnings beat expectations as the media giant's parks and streaming businesses continued to deliver strong growth while the company focused on streamlining operations.
The stock rose 2% in early trading as investors homed in on plans to cut costs by roughly $3 billion by 2029.
"Most of the savings will be used to fund future growth," new CEO Josh D'Amaro told investors on the earnings call. "Now, changes like these are not easy, and they affect people … these steps are important if we want to be a company that moves faster, adapts to a rapidly changing environment, and keeps investing in the content and technology that will drive our growth."
Disney's cost-cutting efforts follow the company's late-September job cuts of approximately 300 roles across human resources and tech. The company said it is using artificial intelligence to accelerate pre- and postproduction processes, design planning around experiences, and operations.
In fiscal Q4, Disney posted adjusted earnings per share of $1.77, above the $1.68 Wall Street expected, alongside revenue of $25.9 billion, which was slightly above the $25.2 billion forecast, according to Bloomberg consensus data.
"Our strong fiscal 2026 results, delivered amid a challenging macroeconomic environment, show we are succeeding on that mission [to be the world's leading entertainment company]," D'Amaro wrote in a shareholder letter.
Total operating income for the company grew 43% year over year to $5 billion, above the expected $4.9 billion, which was the guidance Disney shared last quarter.
For the full year, the company reported revenue of $102.3 billion, alongside adjusted earnings per share of $7.02. Both metrics beat the Street's expectations of $101.5 billion in sales and $6.93 in adjusted earnings per share.
Disney also announced a 33% increase in its dividend to $2 per share, with $1 paid on Jan. 22, 2027, and the rest paid on July 13, 2027.
For 2027, Disney expects segment operating income to grow in the high single digits across Experiences, Entertainment, and Sports. Disney guided for double-digit growth in adjusted earnings per share, assuming "no material deterioration of the global macroeconomic environment."
For the first quarter, Disney expects total segment operating income of approximately $5.4 billion.
Parks and streaming strength drives results
Overall revenue from the Disney Experiences segment, which includes US parks and experiences and the expanding Disney Cruise Line portfolio, came in higher than expected at a record $10.1 billion, above the $9.9 billion forecast.

item.title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says he'd be 'honored' to return to the company
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says he'd be 'honored' to return to the company
2026-11-18
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/former-nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-says-hed-be-honored-to-return-to-the-company-163107005.html
Former Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang says he would be "honored" to return as chief executive of the company he co-founded.
In a post on X Tuesday, Huang apologized to his family again and commented on the support he's seen among former employees, customers, and others seeking to have the company's board reinstate him.
A person familiar with the matter told Yahoo Finance that Nvidia's board is not looking to bring Huang back.
"Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," he wrote.
"Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."
Read more: Buy Nvidia stock or wait? A guide to making the call on any stock.
Huang resigned late last week following revelations of multiple affairs, including one allegedly involving a suspected Chinese spy. Two other affairs were allegedly with Nvidia employees. This is his first public statement since the scandal erupted.
Nvidia has named CFO Colette Kress the company's interim CEO.
Huang's resignation has raised questions about whether Nvidia will continue its prodigious investments across the AI industry, how it will define its roadmap in the years ahead, and more.
The company has shed hundreds of billions of dollars in its market valuation since the scandals erupted.
Huang is now scheduled to appear before closed-door sessions of Congress on Dec. 1 to discuss his reported relationship with the alleged spy, Alice Huang.
The company is scheduled to report its Q3 earnings after the bell today.

item.title: Nvidia board needs 'some heavyweights,' ex-Medtronic CEO Bill George says
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Nvidia board needs 'some heavyweights,' ex-Medtronic CEO Bill George says
2026-11-17
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/nvidia-board-needs-some-heavyweights-ex-medtronic-ceo-bill-george-says-191935557.html
The embattled Nvidia (NVDA) board should have two trains running on the same tracks right now.
One train is out searching for the next CEO.
The other is looking for more experienced board members to ensure a profitable future for a company that continues to be the main cog in the AI wheel.
"They need to add some CEOs, former CEOs to their board, some heavyweights, some people with strong tech backgrounds to their board, because they've got to choose someone," former Medtronic CEO Bill George said on Sozzi Unleashed.
George has served on some of the most high-profile boards in corporate America, including Target (TGT), Goldman Sachs (GS), and ExxonMobil (XOM).
Jensen Huang was ousted as CEO of the company he founded in 1993 amid a shocking turn of events.
According to the New York Times, Huang, whose relationship with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy has embroiled Nvidia in scandal, also had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, one of Huang's 60 or so direct reports.
Reuters reported last Thursday that Huang had a relationship with another Nvidia employee, whose name was not released. Huang has been married to his wife, Lori, for more than 40 years.
While Nvidia looks for a successor, the board has installed longtime CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO ahead of the company's earnings release on Tuesday.
"I think they're going to have to have someone [as CEO] who really digs in and understands the technology," George added. "Don't make the mistake Boeing did with four or five successive CEOs. They got fired because they didn't understand the business. Finally, Boeing got Kelly Ortberg. So this could be a real problem unless they beef up their board and with people that understand it."

item.title: The S&P 500’s shot at 4 straight double-digit years is in Nvidia’s hands
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
The S&P 500’s shot at 4 straight double-digit years is in Nvidia’s hands
2026-11-17
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/the-sp-500s-shot-at-4-straight-double-digit-years-is-in-nvidias-hands-191852498.html
Stocks are within reach of their fourth straight year of double-digit gains, the first since the 1990s dot-com boom. Apple (AAPL) is doing the heavy lifting, while Nvidia (NVDA) could still cost the S&P 500 (^GSPC) its four-peat.
The S&P 500 closed Monday up about 8% for 2026, roughly 110 points shy of the 7,530 or so it needs to end the year with a 10% gain. It had just closed above that line as recently as Friday.
BofA's Michael Hartnett counts only three such streaks since 1871, according to a BofA Global Research report. Those came during World War II, right after it, and in the late-1990s internet boom, when the index "logged 5 straight years" of 10%-plus gains.
Apple carries, Nvidia drags
Apple has added about 125 points to the S&P 500 this year, more than any other stock, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Chipmakers Micron (MU) and AMD (AMD) come next, at about 50 points each.
Nvidia sits at the other end. Its slide has subtracted about 75 points, roughly two-thirds of the gap between Monday's close and the 10% line. Tesla (TSLA), Oracle (ORCL), and Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) have each taken away about 25 to 40 points.
Nvidia gets the next say
Nvidia reports its third quarter results after the close on Nov. 17, its first report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO.
At about 6% of the index, according to Carson Group's Sonu Varghese, every 10% move in Nvidia is worth roughly 40 points. Even a big post-earnings jump couldn't close the roughly 110-point gap alone.
The rest of the market has already done its part. More than half of S&P 500 stocks are up at least 10% this year.
Since the S&P 500's Oct. 6 record, chip stocks have shed about $5.5 trillion in market value, more than the roughly $3.7 trillion the whole index has lost. Gains in Apple and Eli Lilly (LLY) have softened the blow.
"I don't think the stock market overall is expensive," Pershing Square CEO Bill Ackman said at Yahoo Finance Invest. "I think there are a lot of stocks that have been obliterated and are at attractive valuations."
DoubleLine's Jeffrey Gundlach isn't buying it. He recommends "only 30% in equities" until the S&P 500's price-to-earnings ratio falls below 15.
History still gives the bulls a shot
Since 1928, the S&P 500 had been up 10% or more by mid-November in 45 years, and every one of them finished with a double-digit gain, by Yahoo Finance calculations. This year was in that club at Friday's close.
From here, the index needs to gain about 1.5% by Dec. 31. Since 1990, it has done that over the final six weeks in 20 of 36 years.

item.title: Kindness 'compounds': Warren Buffett donates $5.5 billion to family foundations
item.author: Paige Oamek
item.description:
Kindness 'compounds': Warren Buffett donates $5.5 billion to family foundations
2026-11-17
Por Paige Oamek
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/kindness-compounds-warren-buffett-donates-55-billion-to-family-foundations-175818772.html
It's the season for giving.
Billionaire Warren Buffett announced on Monday that he will give 9.225 million Class B Berkshire Hathaway (BRK-B) shares — or roughly $5.5 billion — to four philanthropic foundations this Thanksgiving.
In his annual Thanksgiving letter, Buffett said he will give 3.69 million shares to the Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation, named after his late wife. He will split 1.845 million shares between his three children's philanthropic ventures: the Sherwood Foundation, the Howard G. Buffett Foundation, and NoVo Foundation.
"My children have given thoughtfully to worthy causes for decades, and I trust 100% both their abilities and their fidelity," the 96-year-old wrote.
This year's donation is more than four times greater than the amount set aside for charity last year. In July, the "Oracle from Omaha" promised to donate more than 99% of his entire Berkshire Hathaway fortune — more than $160 billion — to good causes by 2034 through these foundations.
"Last Thanksgiving I wrote that kindness is costless but also priceless," Buffett wrote in his letter on Monday. "A year later, I would only add that it compounds, and at a better rate than anything Charlie and I ever bought."
Read more: 7 creative ways to give money as a gift
In September, Buffett stepped down as chair of Berkshire Hathaway, marking the end of his 50-plus-year tenure. He remains on the board of directors.
In his Thanksgiving letter, he encouraged others to give this holiday season.
"Much of my good fortune has come in the form of people who were kind to me and expected nothing in return. I'm grateful to every one of them," Buffett wrote. "This Thanksgiving, thank one of those selfless people in your own life. Better yet, be a benefactor for someone else."

item.title: Marc Andreessen says government regulation will save jobs from AI — at the cost of economic growth
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Marc Andreessen says government regulation will save jobs from AI — at the cost of economic growth
2026-11-17
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/marc-andreessen-says-government-regulation-will-save-jobs-from-ai--at-the-cost-of-economic-growth-214918442.html
Venture capitalist Marc Andreessen, co-head of Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's task force on jobs and productivity, predicted that artificial intelligence will have a dual effect in the job market: Job losses in government-regulated sectors will be insulated from major job losses, but those regulations will limit economic and productivity growth.
"You might interpret this as good news because it means a revolution is not going to destroy all the jobs or kill everybody," he said. "You could also view this as very negative, which is productivity growth just simply may not grow very much. Economic growth just simply may not grow very much."
Andreessen sees two categories of economic sectors: fast-moving sectors that see rapid technological and economic change, along with rapid job turnover — industries like consumer electronics and media entertainment. The other sectors are a combination of law and government, which are not structured to change rapidly and are typically characterized by extensive subsidization.
That means the fastest-growing sectors will see their prices go down, while the slower-growing regulated or government-subsidized sectors will see their prices go up.
"Your iPhone's getting cheaper, the flat-screen TV on your wall is getting cheaper. The bad news is college education is going to cost a million bucks, healthcare is becoming unaffordable, and good luck buying a house," he said.

item.title: Eli Lilly is trouncing Nvidia — and the weight-loss drug trade is beating AI again
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Eli Lilly is trouncing Nvidia — and the weight-loss drug trade is beating AI again
2026-11-17
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/eli-lilly-is-trouncing-nvidia--and-the-weight-loss-drug-trade-is-beating-ai-again-170530198.html
Wall Street put the AI trade on a diet six weeks ago. The maker of Zepbound has been doing the bulking up.
Since its Oct. 6 record, Nvidia (NVDA) has shed nearly $2 trillion in market value. Eli Lilly (LLY) has added more than $250 billion over the same stretch, a gain topped only by Apple (AAPL) among the market's biggest stocks.
That's a 24% gain for the maker of Zepbound and Mounjaro against a 35% drop for the AI chip king through Monday's close, a day before Nvidia's first earnings report since Jensen Huang's exit.
And it's not just one matchup. The AI trade has been bleeding from every direction since Nvidia peaked, with Alphabet (GOOGL) shedding nearly $790 billion in market value, SpaceX (SPCX) about $470 billion and Micron (MU) about $370 billion, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Apple, Lilly, and Walmart (WMT) have been collecting.
It's the same lineup that showed up in October, when AI stocks lost about $5 trillion in less than a month and Lilly topped the winners' list.
Remember the GLP-1 trade?
Early in this bull market, the weight-loss drugmakers were Wall Street's other obsession. In the 15 months after the October 2022 low, Lilly and Novo Nordisk (NVO) gained about 92% on average, within shouting distance of the Magnificent Seven's 101%.
Then it fell apart. Novo lost about three-quarters of its value from its June 2024 peak, and the GLP-1 trade spent two years watching Big Tech run off with the bull market.
Now the roles have reversed. Lilly just pulled ahead of Nvidia over the past five years. The price tags have flipped too, with Lilly at roughly 27 times forward earnings, about two and a half times Nvidia's multiple, according to Yahoo Finance data.
The two worlds collided last week. In a video pitching Anthropic's IPO, CEO Dario Amodei said, "Cancer, Alzheimer's, heart disease, mental illness — these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade."
Lilly CEO Dave Ricks wasn't buying it. "I think that would be amazing and I think it's not likely," he wrote on X, adding that "progress will likely be steady and incremental."
Lilly's run looks stretched
That doesn't necessarily make the weight-loss trade the one to chase now. Lilly stock sits about 30% above its 200-day moving average, the average of its last 200 closing prices.
Running that hot is nothing new for Lilly in this bull market. It's happened about one in seven trading days, nearly three times as often as in the years before. In 2023 and early 2024, even hotter streaks ended in dips of 7% to 12%. The last two ended in drops of more than 20%.

item.title: The Fed seems to be getting worried about AI
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
The Fed seems to be getting worried about AI
2026-11-17
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/the-fed-seems-to-be-getting-worried-about-ai-110000457.html
Thinking through the potential consequences of the AI revolution isn't explicitly part of the Fed's dual mandate.
But the sweeping impacts of AI, and all the corners of the economy that the emerging technology is set to disrupt, have drawn increasing scrutiny from central bankers.
On Monday, Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh kicked off the first task force hearing on how AI could juice GDP growth or lead to higher unemployment.
Warsh notably did not take the posture of industry booster or tech critic. "Our role in all this is neither advocacy nor opposition," Warsh said. "Our job is to prepare for whatever comes next."
That means focusing on AI's possible impacts and considering different outcomes, ranging from broad-based economic gains to massive job displacement to an AI letdown and productivity slump.
Warsh noted that AI might be different from other paradigm-shifting technologies because of its propensity to generate new ideas and speed up the pace of innovation.
In the best scenario, Warsh told the Fed conference in San Francisco, the technology could lead "to an increase in productivity and economic gains that are shared broadly across labor and the owners of capital. In that event, real GDP growth rises persistently above its long-run average, and the US stays close to full employment."
But given the Fed's specific objectives — inflation and employment — the risks overshadowed the optimism.
Warsh said that the potential for higher unemployment and the dangers of bad actors using AI for nefarious purposes could be "highly disruptive and economically costly."
The chair also referred to AI using the language preferred by Donald Trump and Elon Musk, calling it "super intelligence."
Other central bankers went further. Federal Reserve governor Michael Barr on Monday laid out an array of risks posed by AI. He elaborated on the dangers posed to the financial system if AI technology continues to advance and is widely adopted, such as AI-fueled bank runs, AI trading models that encourage herd-like behavior, and security concerns around autonomous agents exploiting vulnerabilities.
Follow Hamza Shaban on X @hshaban.

item.title: Nvidia is being pulled in opposite directions by 2 powerful forces
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Nvidia is being pulled in opposite directions by 2 powerful forces
2026-11-17
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/nvidia-is-being-pulled-in-opposite-directions-by-2-powerful-forces-110000361.html
Everyone's social feeds are a little different. So depending on your own views towards China, open-weight AI models, Silicon Valley founders, and the role of Big Tech in society, the idea of Jensen Huang returning to Nvidia (NVDA) is a brilliant, righteous comeback, a threat to national security, or the height of corporate irresponsibility.
Nvidia is reportedly waving off the comeback. Its efforts are directed instead to the investigation into Huang and navigating a regulatory landscape that's more hostile to Chinese competition. But regardless of the company's public posture, it is being pulled in opposite directions by very powerful forces.
Much of the tech world is clamoring for Huang's return. Meanwhile, members of Congress are sharpening their oversight knives. And in an extraordinary show of Cabinet infighting, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accused Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick of failing to block China from getting ahold of Nvidia's most advanced chips.
Part of what has made Huang's reported affairs and resignation such a big story is that the saga contains so many competing storylines.
A sex scandal with the power to rattle the S&P 500 has the narrative juice to entice your politics-brained dad, your day-trading brother, and your Real Housewives-obsessed bestie.
But the varying interests drawing people to the story also highlight political and financial tensions that make Nvidia so important to the economy.
Huang is simultaneously occupying the role of founder hero, traitor to his country, China dove whipping boy, and free-market bulwark.
The competing narratives are proving too much for the stock. Tickers typically aren't supposed to become the stage for so much messiness. At least 10 analysts downgraded their Buy rating on Nvidia to Hold. Shares are down roughly 13% over the past week.
An earnings call after the bell will attract even more attention. Investors expect some clarity on the status of the search for a permanent CEO and Nvidia's role in China's acquisition of advanced AI tech. And, given the quarter's high expectations, like revenue nearly doubling from the same period last year, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus, the results will no doubt underscore the opposing forces pulling on the company.
Follow Hamza Shaban on X @hshaban.

Investors expect some clarity on the status of the search for a permanent CEO and Nvidia's role in China's acquisition of advanced AI tech. And, given the quarter's high expectations, like revenue nearly doubling from the same period last year, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus, the results will no doubt underscore the opposing forces pulling on the company.
Follow Hamza Shaban on X @hshaban.

item.title: SpaceX's Starship feat should remind investors that the company at its 'core' is a rocket builder
item.author: Pras Subramanian
item.description:
SpaceX's Starship feat should remind investors that the company at its 'core' is a rocket builder
2026-11-17
Por Pras Subramanian
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/spacexs-starship-feat-should-remind-investors-that-the-company-at-its-core-is-a-rocket-builder-153734886.html
It was a massive day for SpaceX (SPCX) — and the rocket industry.
On Saturday, the company "caught" the upper stage, or Starship, of its largest rocket for the first time. The mission — Starship 15 — took off on Friday night, with Starship deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites and orbiting Earth several times before returning to Starbase, Texas, where it was caught by the Mechazilla platform.
It wasn't a perfect launch, as the lower-stage Super Heavy booster experienced an issue and had to abort its catch. CEO Elon Musk said the Super Heavy booster was slightly low on fuel, hence the abort, but that anomaly is essentially a "footnote in an otherwise historic mission," William Blair analyst Louie DiPalma wrote on Monday morning.
DiPalma added, "In our view, this Starship catch will take the throne for the most famous catch in history from Willie Mays 1954 World Series catch in Major League Baseball's fall classic."
Evercore ISI analyst Kutgun Maral wrote that the Starship 15 launch should remind investors that SpaceX is, at its "core," a rocket builder, and that should underpin much of its value.
"While the never-ending SpaceX newsflow and its stock implications keep us busy day to day, the long-term value of this company will be decided less by the next GW of compute or the next contract renewal than by the cost and frequency of access to orbit," Maral wrote in a note to investors. "That is why Starship has been at the center of our thesis since our initiation — it underpins aspirations for broadband, mobile, orbital compute and, ultimately, the mission itself."
But it was also a "tale of two cities" for the space sector this weekend, as Blair's DiPalma said, flagging United Launch Alliance's setback with its Vulcan rocket on Sunday, with an "anomaly" leading to a lost rocket.
The Vulcan rocket, ULA's newest, lost all 40 Amazon Leo (Project Kuiper) broadband internet satellites on board. ULA is a joint venture between Boeing (BA) and Lockheed Martin (LMT).
"We will work closely with our customer and other appropriate organizations to find the cause, determine the appropriate corrective action, and return to flight as quickly as possible," ULA said in a statement.
"ULA's struggles have taken place during an era in which SpaceX has perfected reusable launch. Over the past 3 years, the Vulcan system has completed 4 successful missions compared with nearly 500 for SpaceX," DiPalma wrote.
Prior to this weekend's mishap, ULA achieved more than 150 consecutive successful launches before experiencing its first total mission failure on Sunday.

item.title: Trump acknowledges 'different views' among aides as his administration advances new limits on semiconductor exports
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Trump acknowledges 'different views' among aides as his administration advances new limits on semiconductor exports
2026-11-17
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/trump-acknowledges-different-views-among-aides-as-his-administration-advances-new-limits-on-semiconductor-exports-163639680.html
Trump acknowledges 'different views' among aides as his administration advances new limits on semiconductor exports
The Trump administration announced on Monday that it is moving to close a perceived loophole in US export controls for advanced semiconductors as bipartisan questions about the role of Nvidia (NVDA) in possible national security lapses intensify.
The raging debate has split the Trump administration over how the US government should respond to the scandal at the chipmaker, with President Trump acknowledging that there are "two different views" among his aides.
Trump said some are leery of insulting China with harsh new restrictions, while others want to crack down. The president said he will make the final decision about how his government approaches the issue.
"I don't think you want to insult China just before you get there," Trump added before he departed for a trip to Asia that includes a China stop. "We're having a very good relationship with China right now." He did not address the new export rules directly.
The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, which oversees export control measures, advanced a rule to limit China's ability to access advanced chips that reside in data centers outside its borders.
The "interim final rule," the release noted, was "written by and at the direction of the Department of Treasury and the National Security Council" and moves the restrictions one step closer to being enacted.
The rules would limit access to sensitive American technology by cracking down on remote computing arrangements that allow Chinese companies to rent computing power in third countries.
It is a move to close what many see as a loophole that has allowed China to sidestep bans and access advanced chips provided by companies like Nvidia.
The announcement from Secretary Howard Lutnick's Commerce Department came as Lutnick faces bipartisan questions on whether he has slow-walked efforts in recent years to limit chip exports and even drawn criticism from other members of the Trump Cabinet.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has notably declined to defend Lutnick's actions in a series of recent television appearances. On Fox News on Sunday, Bessent also discussed what he termed a "culture of noncompliance" at Nvidia, which he said led to semiconductor exports potentially ending up in Chinese hands.
Bessent said Nvidia needs "a dramatic shake-up" and should "go outside the company" as it seeks a new chief executive.
That last point is the subject of dispute among Trump's advisers, with Bessent staking out a sharply critical position while Elon Musk leads a petition to reinstate Huang.
